title: Service cannot boot: published 0.8.1 moved to JSON Schema 2020-12, Ajv is draft-07
description:
BROKEN IN THE WORKING TREE RIGHT NOW. SchemaRegistry.load() throws, and buildApp() calls it at construction, so the process fails at boot.

Reproduced 2026-07-31:
  schema registry: failed to compile 0.8.1 (sha256 290290fd4623d25c3fc18724f317249469e03bee9d64ec39279730d3b3a87470):
  Error: no schema with key or ref "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"

Cause: 0.8.1 was published upstream on 2026-07-30 and the vendored copy was refreshed (src/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.1.json, mtime 2026-07-31 11:42). The published bytes changed dialect:
  HEAD:         "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"
  working tree: "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"

src/schema-registry.ts buildAjv() returns `new Ajv(...)` — Ajv v8 default export validates draft-07 only. A 2020-12 schema needs the `ajv/dist/2020` build. DESIGN.md section 13 also states "Validation: Ajv (draft-07)".

Other changes in the republished 0.8.1 (diff vs HEAD): schemaVersion example finally fixed 0.1.1 -> 0.8.1 (resolves proposal 5 of cce-data-delivery-validator-ven); `transferCallbackUrl` property REMOVED; `callbackUrl` dropped from examples; example record values and ordering changed.

ALSO UNTRACKED AND UNREGISTERED: src/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.2.json (sha256 b6ee10cfb00665ac8c296bee7b39a9ee214a3feecced95cbc080c039f355e15d) is also 2020-12 and is present in the authoring folder. It is inert today because VENDORED in schema-registry.ts is an explicit list, not a directory scan — so 0.8.2 is NOT auto-discovered and currently does nothing.

Work:
  1. Select the Ajv build PER SCHEMA from the declared $schema, not globally. Each version already compiles in its own Ajv instance, so this is a per-entry choice and mixed-dialect registries keep working (0.8.0 stays draft-07).
  2. Register 0.8.2 and decide whether it becomes currentVersion().
  3. Update DESIGN.md section 13 which hardcodes "Ajv (draft-07)".
  4. Add a regression test that compiles EVERY vendored version, so a dialect change fails a test rather than only failing at boot.
  5. Re-verify the content hashes surfaced as blessed-bytes provenance.

NOTE the docs/ copy was NOT refreshed: docs/cce-interop-0.8.1.json is still the old draft-07 bytes (sha256 cf2a7503...), so docs/ and src/schemas/ now genuinely disagree for the first time. Decide whether docs/ stays a mirror or stops being a schema location at all.
acceptance_criteria: SchemaRegistry.load() succeeds with the published 0.8.1 and 0.8.2 registered; a test compiles every vendored version; DESIGN.md no longer claims a single draft-07 dialect; docs/ vs src/schemas/ divergence resolved deliberately.
notes:
FIXED 2026-07-31. Scoped to 0.8.1 only per direction; 0.8.2 was removed from src/schemas by the user and is explicitly out of scope until published.

What landed:
- schema-registry.ts: buildAjv() now returns Ajv2020 from ajv/dist/2020.js (NAMED import - the default export of that CJS build types as a namespace under NodeNext and is not constructable). strict:false and allErrors:true preserved.
- VENDORED reduced to 0.8.1 alone; pre-release 0.8.0 dropped (draft-07, never used off this machine). Mixed-dialect per-entry Ajv selection deliberately NOT built - documented in the module header as the seam to add if a second dialect ever returns.
- schema-registry.test.ts: EXPECTED_SHA256 -> 290290fd...; the two-version assertions rewritten. The "own Ajv instance" test is now a LOOP over supportedVersions() asserting every vendored version compiles and has distinct blessed bytes - it is the regression guard for exactly this bug (dialect change caught by a test, not only at boot) and re-acquires its teeth automatically when a second version registers.
- schema-stage.test.ts: simple 0.8.0 payload strings -> 0.8.1. The two OUTDATED tests could no longer work (single vendored version = nothing older than current), so they now use registryWithNewerCurrent(), a stub delegating to the real registry but reporting synthetic version 9.9.9 as current. postToSession() grew an optional registry param that feeds BuildAppOptions.registry, so the full-flow outdated test drives the real HTTP path.
- DESIGN.md: section 13 dialect line corrected; section 9 no longer claims the registry is seeded with 0.8.0, and now states the registry is a POLICY about accepted versions.
- docs/cce-interop-0.8.1.json re-synced to the published bytes; all three copies (docs/, src/schemas/, authoring folder) are byte-identical again at 290290fd... The structural question of whether docs/ should hold schemas at all remains open in dkz.5.

Verified: registry loads (0.8.1 current); tsc clean; 217 tests / 178 pass / 0 fail / 39 skipped (unchanged Postgres-gated skips); eslint + prettier clean; npm run build succeeds; buildApp() boots and GET /health returns 200.

LOOSE END for a maintainer decision: src/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.0.json is still on disk but unregistered, and scripts/copy-schemas.mjs copies the whole directory, so it still ships into dist/schemas/. Harmless but dead weight - delete the file, or teach copy-schemas to copy only registered versions.
PROVENANCE CORRECTION + VERIFICATION 2026-07-31. Earlier notes said the vendored 0.8.1 matched "the published bytes". At the time that was NOT verified - only repo-to-repo agreement across five local copies. The publication URL is NOT the $id host: real location is https://docs.2to8.cc/cce-data-interop/schemas/cce-interop-<version>.json (schemas.2to8.cc does not resolve at all).

NOW VERIFIED by fetching the live artifact: HTTP 200, 45340 bytes, sha256 290290fd4623d25c3fc18724f317249469e03bee9d64ec39279730d3b3a87470 - BYTE-IDENTICAL to src/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.1.json. The DESIGN section 9 blessed-bytes claim holds for 0.8.1 against the live published artifact.
close_reason: Fixed: registry compiles the published 0.8.1 under Ajv's 2020-12 build; 0.8.0 dropped; regression test added; app boots and full build/test/lint are green.

title: Public UI never states synthetic/sandbox data only
description:
The web UI carries no warning that this service accepts SYNTHETIC TEST DATA ONLY. A grep of all of src/web/ for synthetic|sandbox|test data|real data|production returns ZERO hits.

This is a safety issue, not a copy issue. DESIGN.md section 2 makes "receiving real production data" an explicit non-goal, and section 12 justifies the entire capability-URL design ONLY by that constraint: "The UUID is a bearer capability... URLs leak via logs, proxies, and browser history. Acceptable for synthetic test data (v1 only data). If real data is ever in scope, revisit."

Failure mode on publication: a supplier points a live CCE fleet at the endpoint. Real facility and device data then sits behind a URL the design itself calls leakable, under a 7-day retention window, with possession-equals-authority access. Nothing in the product tells them not to.

Needs the warning in at least three places:
  1. Landing page (src/web/routes/Landing.tsx) - above or beside the Create test endpoint button, before they commit.
  2. Dashboard Setup card (src/web/components/Setup.tsx) - adjacent to the ingest URL and curl snippet, at the moment of integration.
  3. README (see the README child issue).

Consider also echoing it in the ingest success response body, which DESIGN.md section 6 already calls a teaching surface.
acceptance_criteria: Landing page and dashboard Setup card both state prominently that the endpoint is for synthetic/test data only and must not receive real CCE or PII data. Wording is consistent with DESIGN.md sections 2 and 12.
close_reason: b95026e — synthetic-data-only warning on Landing, Setup card, and ingest response body (shared SyntheticDataNotice component); review clean

title: NEXT BITE: docs truth sweep — DESIGN.md (dkz.6, 3yu, 5zm) + CLAUDE.md drift claims (dkz.5)

Rewrite §8 to state implemented reality and reference that a write-side cap is under consideration — do not silently decide cap-vs-no-cap either way.
- Status line: promote from "Draft" to wording fit for a public audience (e.g. "Living document — v1 scope locked"); keep the locked-decisions authority framing. Whether §7 surfaces in README belongs to dkz.2 — note it there if you have an opinion, don't do it.

## Slicing recommendation

Check `git -C .. rev-parse` first: if the workspace is not a git repo, edit the file and say so in the report; if it IS somehow tracked, commit separately there. Keep the relative-path rule (that file's own rule) intact.

title: NEXT BITE: TxDetail compression cell (5bs.2) + raw JSON inspector (5bs.3)
description:

title: NEXT BITE: Bearer auth (5bs.4) + auth-method picker (dav)
description:
## Underlying issues

- cce-data-delivery-validator-5bs.4: Support Bearer token authentication (RFC 6750) — third DS01.3 auth method end-to-end (DDL, credential parsing, ingest stage, dashboard opt-in, grading).
- cce-data-delivery-validator-dav: §1.3 guidance says "pick the header-token or HTTP Basic method" but Setup offers no picker (Setup.tsx:141 calls enableAuth with no body; service defaults to header). The picker built for 5bs.4 resolves this; dav is dep-blocked behind 5bs.4.

## Read first

- `bd show` both issues in full.
- src/auth/credential.ts, src/ingest/stages/auth.ts, db/initdb/10-session.sql (auth_method CHECK), the enableAuth flow in src/api/ + src/web/api.ts + src/web/components/Setup.tsx.
- src/web/components/requirementReference.ts entry 1.3 — as rewritten by 81f0b05 (see context below).

## Recently-decided context

- 81f0b05 (closed 5bs.5) made every REQUIREMENT_REFERENCE `text` a VERBATIM quote of the 2025 requirements PDF, which names only TWO auth methods. Do NOT add Bearer to the 1.3 `text` — that would break verbatim fidelity. The third method is a DS01.3 addition: describe it in the `guidance` field (which is where editorializing belongs), consistent with the file-header discipline. Keep 2025 numbering (locked decision; docs/clause-mapping.md maps DS01.3).
- dav was filed because the NEW 1.3 guidance says suppliers pick a method while no picker exists. Building the picker satisfies both; verify the guidance sentence ends up true.
- Reviewer noted src/web/api.ts:251 comment calls the header-method secret a "bearer token" — same conflation; fix that comment while in there.
- `npm run lint` is red at HEAD from gitignored docs/internal/ (bd y5u). Gate on `npx eslint src` + `npx prettier --check src` instead, plus `npm test` and `npm run build`.
- House rule: widening the auth_method CHECK needs a NEW numbered file under db/initdb/ — never edit an existing DDL file in place. Postgres tests auto-skip without docker; if `docker compose up -d postgres` works in this environment, run the DB-gated tests too (note initdb only runs on first boot — a pre-existing volume will not pick up the new DDL file; document how the widening applies to existing deployments, e.g. the new file is written to be safe to apply manually).

## Slicing recommendation

1. **Subagent A — backend**
   - Reads: src/auth/credential.ts (+ tests), src/ingest/stages/auth.ts, src/api/ session/auth routes, db/initdb/.
   - Produces: new numbered DDL file widening auth_method to include bearer; Bearer parse/verify in credential.ts dispatching on the Authorization scheme token (shares the header with Basic — dispatch on scheme, not header presence); PresentedCredential mapping in stages/auth.ts; API accepts an auth method choice on the §1.3 opt-in call (default stays header for back-compat); tests for all of it.
   - Acceptance: a Bearer-configured session accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and rejects wrong/missing tokens; header/basic behavior unchanged; tests green.
   - Commit referencing 5bs.4.
2. **Subagent B — frontend + reference text** (after A's commit)
   - Reads: A's commit, src/web/components/Setup.tsx, src/web/api.ts, requirementReference.ts.
   - Produces: auth-method picker (header / basic / bearer) in the §1.3 opt-in UI emitting the right curl/config snippet per method; api.ts passes the chosen method (and fixes the :251 comment); 1.3 guidance updated to name the DS01.3 Bearer addition WITHOUT touching the verbatim 2025 `text`; guidance's "pick a method" claim now true (resolves dav).
   - Acceptance: 5bs.4's criteria ("all three methods offered and described accurately") + dav's complaint gone; web typecheck/build green.
   - Commit referencing 5bs.4 and dav.

Run order: serial (A then B — B consumes A's API contract). Nothing parallel.

## Out of scope

- 5bs.2 / 5bs.3 (detail-pane compression + payload inspector) — separate bites.
- README (dkz.2) and any docs/ churn.
- Do not edit existing db/initdb files or existing REQUIREMENT_REFERENCE `text` quotes.

## Commit + test expectations

- Commit in this repo when green; terse imperative style per `git log --oneline`; bd ids in messages; do not push; do not commit .beads state (manager handles export).

title: Transmissions panel is far taller than the design mock; cap it at ~10 rows
description:
The scrollable transmissions list works, but its height is significantly larger than the Claude design mock-ups intended. Because the docked detail pane sits BELOW the list, an oversized list pushes the detail pane far down the page and often out of view — which partially reinstates the very problem the master-detail redesign was meant to fix.

Fix: the list region should be tall enough to show ROUGHLY 10 transmissions, no more.

Current implementation (src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx): the list region is sized proportionally — `flex: 1 1 56%` on the scroll container — so its height follows the cards height rather than a row count. A proportional rule cannot express "about ten rows".

Considerations:
  - Rows are NOT fixed height: the card uses estimateSize + measureElement from @tanstack/react-virtual because row chrome wraps. So "10 rows" is approximate and should be derived from the estimated row height, not hardcoded in pixels and left to drift.
  - Keep the list scrollable and keep virtualization — this is a sizing change, not a paging change.
  - Verify the detail pane remains visible without page scrolling at common viewport heights once the cap is in.
  - Cross-check against design_handoff_scale_at_volume/ (and the earlier redesign handoff it references) for the intended proportions before picking a number.
acceptance_criteria: The transmissions list shows about ten rows before scrolling, and the docked detail pane is visible without scrolling the page at normal viewport heights.
close_reason: c5df62c — list capped at ROW_ESTIMATE_PX*10 (370px), flex 0 1 auto; detail pane above the fold at 800px; review clean, P3 follow-up 5bs.7

title: requirementReference.ts misquotes the requirements document
description:
src/web/components/requirementReference.ts renders authoritative-looking spec language in the dashboard drill-down. Several entries do not match the source document (docs/Interoperable CCE Data Delivery - REQUIREMENTS - 20250330 .pdf). Suppliers will read these as the requirement.

Confirmed errors, checked against the 2025 PDF on 2026-07-31:

  4.3 — says "permanent failures (e.g. 501, 505, most 4xx)". The document says: 501, 505, and ALL 4xx EXCEPT 404, 408, 409, and 429. "most 4xx" is vague where the source is exact, and the carve-out is the operationally important part. (This list is UNCHANGED in DS01.3 — the error is ours, not a spec drift.)

  2.2 — says "within minutes of being received FROM THE LOGGER". The document says "within a few minutes after it is received BY THE REMOTE DATA SYSTEM" — i.e. the supplier platform, not the logger. This materially changes what is being measured and feeds the (correct) conclusion that we cannot verify it passively.

  1.3 — says "bearer token (in an agreed header) or HTTP Basic". Conflates the configurable-header token method with the RFC 6750 Bearer scheme, and omits the third method DS01.3 adds. See the sibling Bearer issue.

Audit the remaining 24 entries against the PDF in the same pass rather than fixing only the three found so far. The file header already documents the correct discipline (spec language verbatim, guidance free of session-specific claims) — this is a fidelity failure, not a design one.

Keep 2025 numbering per the 2026-07-31 decision; docs/clause-mapping.md carries the DS01.3 correspondence.
acceptance_criteria: Every entry in REQUIREMENT_REFERENCE has been checked against the 2025 requirements PDF and quotes it faithfully; the three confirmed errors are corrected.
close_reason: 81f0b05 — all 27 entries re-derived verbatim from 2025 PDF; 3 confirmed + ~14 additional fidelity errors fixed; review verified 26/27 verbatim-exact, acceptance met

title: Support Bearer token authentication (RFC 6750)
description:
DS01.3 clause 5.1.5 names THREE authentication methods; the 2025 requirements document named two. The new one is:

  Authorization: Bearer <token>   (RFC 6750)

src/auth/credential.ts supports `header` (token in a configurable header) and `basic` only. session.auth_method in db/initdb/10-session.sql carries a CHECK constraint listing the allowed values, so widening it needs a NEW numbered DDL file — never edit an existing one in place (house rule).

Work:
  - Widen the auth_method CHECK to include `bearer` (new numbered file under db/initdb/).
  - Add Bearer parsing/verification in credential.ts alongside basic. Note it shares the Authorization header with basic, so the stage must dispatch on the scheme token, not on header presence.
  - src/ingest/stages/auth.ts maps request headers into PresentedCredential — extend that mapping.
  - Dashboard section 1.3 opt-in UI must offer Bearer as a third choice and emit the right config snippet.
  - Update REQUIREMENT_REFERENCE["1.3"], whose current text says "bearer token (in an agreed header) or HTTP Basic" — that conflates the configurable-header method with the real Bearer scheme and now names only two of three.

DS01.3 also adds "The employer shall specify the desired method and supply the credentials", which the existing dashboard-generates-the-credential flow already satisfies.
acceptance_criteria: A supplier can opt into Bearer auth from the dashboard; the endpoint enforces it; section 1.3 grades from real traffic; all three DS01.3 methods are offered and described accurately.
close_reason: 9231ca3 + e50a572 — Bearer auth end-to-end (DDL 50-session-auth-bearer.sql, scheme-dispatched verification, API method param, 3-way Setup picker, 1.3 guidance); review: both acceptance MET, P3 follow-up 5zm

title: Surface compression (none|gzip) in the transmission detail pane
description:
content_encoding is already persisted (db/initdb/20-transmission.sql), already returned by the API (toTransmissionView in src/api/sessions.ts), and never rendered. The TxDetail meta grid in src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx shows only transferId, schema, bytes, type.

Add a fourth/fifth cell labelled `compression` (NOT `content_encoding` — user specified the label) with values:
  none   when content_encoding is null/absent
  gzip   when content_encoding is gzip

Decide how to render a value that is neither — an unexpected or illegal Content-Encoding is exactly the section 1.6 signal, so it should be visible rather than coerced to `none`. Suggest showing the raw value and letting the existing 1.6 finding carry the verdict.

Note payload SIZE is already shown ("bytes" cell) — that half of the original request is done.
acceptance_criteria: TxDetail shows a `compression` field reading none or gzip; a non-gzip encoding is visibly distinguishable from none.
close_reason: fffae12 — compression cell + raw JSON inspector with pointer highlighting; review: both MET; follow-ups vul (decoded-claim accuracy), yn3 (size-bounded wording), 1z9 (phantom cap)

title: Raw JSON payload inspector in the transmission detail pane
description:
Both the parsed payload (body jsonb) and the size-bounded original bytes (raw_body) are already persisted and already returned to the client by toTransmissionView. Nothing in the UI renders either one. This is presentation-only work — no backend or DDL change.

Requirements:
  - Let the user inspect the raw JSON for any selected transmission.
  - raw_body matters most when parsing FAILED and body is NULL — that is the case the drill-down exists for (DESIGN.md sections 8 and 10). Do not render only the pretty-printed parsed body, or the failure case shows nothing.
  - Keep it inside the docked detail pane with its own scroll region; do not let a large payload blow out the pane height (see the sibling panel-height issue).
  - Consider linking schema-error JSON Pointers (finding.instance_path) to the corresponding location in the raw view — the findings already carry the pointers.

title: Section 3.1 is never graded; give it the conditional check it is actually for
description:
No pipeline stage ever emits a finding with requirement 3.1. It exists only as a static row in src/api/compliance-matrix.ts classed `verified`, so deriveStatus() sees pass=0/fail=0 and returns `untested` forever. The matrix advertises a passive check that does not exist.

DECIDED 2026-07-31 what 3.1 is for. With schema-precedence retained as a house rule, 3.1s STRUCTURAL content is genuinely subsumed by 3.2 — if Ajv passes, the meta block and DS01 object shapes are correct by construction. What Ajv CANNOT express is the CONDITIONAL obligation, and that is what 3.1 should own:

  meta.customDataSchema is required ONLY WHEN the payload carries manufacturer-specific data objects.

That conditional is the substance of DS01.3 clause 5.3.3 (new field) and 5.3.5, so one implementation serves both. Per DS01.2/DS01.3 clause 4.5, manufacturer-specific objects are lower-case and z-prefixed (e.g. ztpcm), which makes them detectable: the 0.8.1 schema has additionalProperties:true in 6 places, so custom objects sail through unexamined today.

Check to implement:
  - Scan the payload for custom (z-prefixed / non-Annex-1) data objects.
  - If present and meta.customDataSchema is absent -> 3.1 FAIL.
  - If present and customDataSchema is present -> 3.1 PASS (we do not fetch or validate the referenced schema; say so).
  - If no custom objects -> 3.1 PASS with a detail saying the conditional did not apply.
  - Optionally flag custom objects that violate the lower-case z-prefix naming rule.

BLOCKED ON: meta.customDataSchema does not exist in cce-interop-0.8.1.json (grep count zero). Check whether the newly published 0.8.1/0.8.2 added it before building against it — if not, this is an upstream gap feeding cce-data-delivery-validator-ven, and the check runs as a semantic stage independent of the schema.

ALSO REQUIRED (explicit user request): the dashboard must EXPLAIN this to the supplier. Update REQUIREMENT_REFERENCE["3.1"] in src/web/components/requirementReference.ts — its current guidance ("The schema enforces the meta block and DS01 object shapes") describes something that emits no findings. New guidance should say plainly that structural conformance is graded under 3.2 and that 3.1 covers the conditional obligations the schema cannot express.
acceptance_criteria: Section 3.1 emits findings from real traffic; the conditional customDataSchema rule is checked; the dashboard guidance for 3.1 explains the division of labour with 3.2 rather than describing a check that does not run.
close_reason: fff4987 — §3.1 graded via schema-independent custom-schema stage (z-prefix detection, conditional customDataSchema duty), matrix+guidance honest; review: acceptance met, P2 follow-ups squ/3yu

title: Document and ship the Caddy edge/proxy contract
description:
DESIGN.md section 4.1 imposes three hard requirements on the TLS-terminating reverse proxy, and NONE of them are documented or shipped. There is no Caddyfile anywhere in the repo, no deployment doc, and no operator-facing note about TRUSTED_PROXY.

The three contract terms:
  1. X-Forwarded-Proto must be set by the proxy; the app trusts it scoped to the proxy address only (Fastify trustProxy, src/app.ts, env TRUSTED_PROXY, default 127.0.0.1). This is how section 1.1 HTTPS is known.
  2. The proxy must NOT impose a request body size cap below the 1MB grading threshold. If it does, oversized POSTs get the proxy generic 413, the transmission is never recorded, and the section 1.4 teaching finding is never emitted. DESIGN.md is explicit that the app owns the section 1.4 cap (src/app.ts raises Fastify bodyLimit to 2 MiB for exactly this reason - see bug 6y3).
  3. The body must reach the app as sent: no request decompression, no re-chunking, so section 1.4 wire-byte measurement and section 1.6 Content-Encoding / double-encoding detection see the supplier exact bytes.

Why this is a publication blocker rather than a nicety: a self-hoster who misses any of these gets no error. They get SILENTLY WRONG conformance verdicts issued to suppliers under this projects name. Wrong grades are worse than no tool.

Deliverables: a checked-in Caddyfile (or documented equivalent) with the contract encoded and commented, plus a deployment/operations section covering TRUSTED_PROXY, the env var surface, and how to verify the contract holds (e.g. a smoke test that POSTs an oversized and a gzipped body and asserts the app - not the proxy - produced the response).
acceptance_criteria: A Caddyfile (or equivalent) is checked in with the section 4.1 contract encoded and commented; operator docs explain TRUSTED_PROXY and how to verify the contract; the failure mode of a misconfigured proxy is stated explicitly.
close_reason: 421ea96 — Caddyfile + deployment.md + smoke-proxy-contract.sh, empirically verified through real Caddy both green and misconfigured-red; review accepted, P3 follow-ups qi9/c64

title: Add LICENSE and fix package.json publication metadata

Also add "license", "repository", "homepage", and a fuller "description" to package.json once the publication target is known.

description:

title: NEXT BITE: signature normalization engine (4h4.3)
description:
## Underlying issues

- cce-data-delivery-validator-4h4.3 (P1): Signature normalization engine — pure src/api/signatures.ts porting engine.js (generalizePath/isIssue/sigKey/sigTitle/computeSignatures/signaturesForReq/txMatchesSig), unit-tested. Its dep 4h4.1 (structured finding fields) is now CLOSED, so the inputs exist.

## Read first

Memories to query:
- `bd memories schema` → schema-registry-0.8.1-current-outdated — the outdated-but-valid §3.2 info finding (outdated:true, code tx.outdated_schema). isIssue() must treat it as a soft issue (info+outdated → grouped).

Documents (authoritative — port VERBATIM in behavior):
- design_handoff_scale_at_volume/redesign/engine.js — the reference computeSignatures/sigKey/sigTitle/generalizePath fold + CODE_TITLE map (lines ~169-260). THE spec.
- 4h4.3's own description — full function-by-function contract + the returned signature shape {key,req,title,kind,sev,count,txCount,sourceCount,first,last,examplePointer}.

## Recently-decided context

Facts established THIS session that engine.js (a prototype) does NOT reflect — a verbatim port will be subtly wrong on all three:

1. **The emitted tx.* code set is a SUPERSET of engine.js's 7-entry CODE_TITLE.** 4h4.1 + the nfp fix landed 14 codes total. engine.js CODE_TITLE only covers 7: tx.missing_charset, tx.body_too_large, tx.parse_failed, tx.duplicate_transfer, tx.outdated_schema, tx.bad_media_type, tx.double_encoded. The 7 NOT in the prototype map: tx.unsupported_encoding, tx.undecodable_body (encoding.ts), tx.missing_schema_version, tx.unsupported_schema_version, tx.schema_invalid (schema.ts), tx.irregular_interval (interval.ts §3.4), tx.concurrent_delivery (concurrency.ts §2.1). EXTEND CODE_TITLE to cover all 14 with sensible labels — otherwise those 7 fall through to the raw detail string (functionally OK, never dropped, but verbose drift-prone titles, which is what signatures exist to avoid). Note: auth §1.3 fail (auth.ts:113) has NO code by design (auth path is out of scope of the code-wiring); it falls to the req+detail fallback — that is acceptable, do not add an auth code here.

2. **Field-name adaptation: the real FindingView is NOT the prototype shape.** engine.js uses f.sev and f.req; the landed view (src/api/sessions.ts toFindingView / src/web/api.ts FindingView) uses **f.severity** and **f.requirement**. The structured fields ARE already camelCase on the view: keyword, instancePath, param, code, plus outdated, detail, pointer. So sigKey/isIssue/sigTitle must read f.severity/f.requirement (+ camelCase structured fields), not f.sev/f.req.

3. **Real inputs replace the prototype's synthetic ones.** Findings come from the per-tx view (TransmissionView.findings: FindingView[]). The source Set for sourceCount keys off **tx.source** (raw transfer_src from 4h4.2; empty string '' is the single stable unknown bucket — keep it as a key, it counts as one source). Timestamps first/last come from **tx.received_at** (ISO string), NOT the prototype's minutes-since-midnight — compare as Date/epoch and emit ISO (or epoch ms) consistently. Keep the FOLD logic identical to engine.js; only the field accessors change.

## Slicing recommendation

1. **Single subagent — Signature engine (4h4.3)**
   - Reads: design_handoff_scale_at_volume/redesign/engine.js (port target), src/web/api.ts (FindingView + TransmissionView field names), src/api/sessions.ts toFindingView (confirm the exact emitted finding fields), src/api/source.ts (how source is derived, for the source Set).
   - Produces: pure src/api/signatures.ts (no DB/HTTP imports) + src/api/signatures.test.ts.
   - Acceptance: matches 4h4.3's acceptance — ports all 7 functions; keys off structured fields not message; array indices generalized + value never in key; computeSignatures returns the pre-aggregated shape sorted by count DESC; CODE_TITLE covers all 14 emitted codes; unit tests cover schema-keyword, check-code, outdated-info, and the index-collapse (/data/0/.. + /data/7/.. → one sig) cases.

Run order: serial, ONE agent. Pure module, no file sharing with anything else — but keep it solo since it is small and tightly specified.

## Out of scope

- Wiring signatures into an endpoint — that is 4h4.4 (scope-aware summary), which this BLOCKS.
- The paginated/filterable list endpoint (4h4.5) — also blocked on this; txMatchesSig is built here but consumed there.
- Trend buckets / sparkline data (4h4.10 / scorecard).
- Do NOT touch the stages, repository, or sessions.ts beyond READING them for field names — this is a new pure module only.

## Commit + test expectations

- Commit locally to this repo (no remote configured — do NOT push) when tested + green. One commit.
- Gates before commit: `npm test`, `npm run typecheck:web`, `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `npm run lint`.
- Terse commit style `<imperative summary> (4h4.3)` (run `git log --oneline` first).
- Close 4h4.3 with `bd close cce-data-delivery-validator-4h4.3 --reason="<sha> …"` when it lands.
close_reason: aa3ed03 Add signature normalization engine — pure src/api/signatures.ts (+test), all 7 functions ported, 14 CODE_TITLE codes, gates green, clean review

title: 4h4.1: heuristic §3.4 interval + §2.1 concurrency fail findings have no stable code
description:
Commit aec5ac6 (4h4.1) added stable tx.* codes to the transport/schema stages but MISSED two heuristic semantic checks that emit severity:'fail' findings:

- src/ingest/stages/semantic/interval.ts:143 — §3.4 reading-cadence-irregular FAIL, no code:
- src/ingest/stages/semantic/concurrency.ts:45 — §2.1 concurrent-delivery FAIL, no code:

The pass branches (interval.ts:132, concurrency.ts:32) correctly need no code.

title: Signature normalization engine (computeSignatures/sigKey/sigTitle)
description:
Implement signature normalization server-side: the pure projection of validator output that collapses identical defects into distinct "issues". Port the reference algorithm from design_handoff_scale_at_volume/redesign/engine.js VERBATIM in behavior (it is the authoritative spec).

WHY: One requirement (esp. §3.2 schema validation) can fail for many unrelated reasons. A requirement-level count cannot answer "what are the distinct things to fix, and how widespread is each?". Signatures can — and because they key off structured fields, they are comprehensive on day one with no catalogue to maintain.

WHAT: A new module (e.g. src/api/signatures.ts), pure (no DB/HTTP), unit-tested. Port these functions exactly:

- `generalizePath(p)` → strip array indices: `(p||'').replace(/\/\d+/g,'/*')` so /data/0/ABST and /data/7/ABST collapse to /data/*/ABST.
- `isIssue(f)` → true if sev==='fail', OR sev==='info' && outdated (outdated schema is a soft issue worth surfacing). Everything else (passes, plain info) is not grouped.
- `sigKey(f)`:
  - if f.keyword: `req + '|' + keyword + '|' + generalizePath(instancePath) + '|' + (param||'')`
  - else if f.code: `req + '|' + code`
  - else: `req + '|' + (detail||'')`  (last-resort fallback)
- `sigTitle(f)` → the only hand-written table (~1 row per Ajv keyword + per check code). Schema keywords: required→"Missing required property {param}", format→"{field} must match format {param}", additionalProperties→"Unexpected property {param}", type→"{field} has the wrong type", enum→"{field} is not an allowed value", minimum/maximum→"{field} out of allowed range", default→detail or "{keyword} at {path}". `field` = last segment of generalizePath(instancePath) or 'document'. Non-schema: CODE_TITLE[f.code] || detail || req, where CODE_TITLE maps each tx.* code to a label (copy the map from engine.js: tx.missing_charset, tx.body_too_large, tx.parse_failed, tx.duplicate_transfer, tx.outdated_schema, tx.bad_media_type, tx.double_encoded). Worst case for an untemplated edge is a plainer title — never a dropped or misfiled issue.
- `computeSignatures(transmissions)` → fold every issue finding into a Map keyed by sigKey, accumulating per signature: `count` (raw findings), `txCount` (DISTINCT transmissions), `sources` (Set of source ids → emit sourceCount), `first`/`last` timestamps, a representative `example` finding, and `pointer`/`examplePointer`. Sort by count DESC. (See the exact fold in engine.js computeSignatures.)
- `signaturesForReq(sigs, reqId)` → filter to one requirement.
- `txMatchesSig(tx, key)` → tx.findings.some(f => isIssue(f) && sigKey(f) === key). Needed by the list cross-filter.

Returned/aggregated signature shape (pre-aggregated for the wire — the browser must NEVER need every raw finding to render the summary): `{ key, req, title, kind: 'schema'|'check', sev, count, txCount, sourceCount, first, last, examplePointer }`.

TWO RULES TO HOLD THE LINE ON (confirmed with the team): (1) generalize the path, drop the value — strip array indices, never put the offending value in the key; ~3 normalization rules total, not per-failure logic. (2) Sign on Ajv's structured fields, not its message string.

INPUT NOTE: in the real app the finding rows come from the DB (structured fields from the structured-findings issue), and timestamps come from the transmission's received_at — not the prototype's minutes-since-midnight. Adapt `first`/`last` accordingly (epoch ms or ISO) but keep the fold logic identical.

OUT OF SCOPE: wiring into an endpoint (separate scope-aware-summary issue) and the trend/sparkline.
acceptance_criteria: pure signatures module ports generalizePath/isIssue/sigKey/sigTitle/computeSignatures/signaturesForReq/txMatchesSig per engine.js; keys off structured fields not message; array indices generalized, value never in key; computeSignatures returns pre-aggregated {key,req,title,kind,sev,count,txCount,sourceCount,first,last,examplePointer} sorted by count DESC; unit tests cover schema + check + outdated-info + collapse cases.

title: Structured finding fields (keyword/instancePath/param/code)
description:
Persist and emit STRUCTURED fields on findings so signatures can be derived robustly. This is the foundation of the whole signature feature: without these fields, signatures can only key off the English message string, which drifts across Ajv versions.

WHY: A signature collapses identical defects into one issue. Its stable key is built from structured fields, never the message (README "Signature normalization", rule 2). Today findings carry only requirement/severity/detail/pointer/outdated.

WHAT (backend, no web layer here):

1. DB migration (db/initdb/30-finding.sql): add nullable columns to `finding`:
   - `keyword text` — Ajv keyword (the defect CLASS: required/format/additionalProperties/type/enum/minimum/maximum/…). NULL for non-schema findings.
   - `instance_path text` — Ajv instancePath (e.g. /data/0/ABST). NULL when not schema.
   - `param text` — the identifying param (missingProperty / format / additionalProperty / enum-of / …) — NOT the offending value. NULL when n/a.
   - `code text` — stable check code for transport/heuristic findings (e.g. tx.missing_charset). NULL for schema findings.
   All nullable, no CHECK churn. Keep existing `outdated` boolean.

2. repository.ts: extend `InsertFindingInput` and `FindingRow` with `keyword?`, `instancePath?`, `param?`, `code?` (camelCase on input, snake_case row). Thread through `insertFinding`, `insertFindings` (the multi-row VALUES builder — bump the per-row param count from 5 to 9 and add the columns), and the SELECT in `listFindingsForSession`.

3. Emit structured fields from the pipeline stages (the Finding type === InsertFindingInput, so stages just add fields):
   - schema.ts (Ajv): for each Ajv ErrorObject set `keyword: err.keyword`, `instancePath: err.instancePath`, and `param` = the identifying param pulled from err.params (missingProperty for `required`, format for `format`, additionalProperty for `additionalProperties`, allowedValues/enum for `enum`, limit for minimum/maximum, type for `type`). The missing/unsupported-schemaVersion fails and the outdated-info finding get `code: tx.outdated_schema` (info) etc. — see B-codes below.
   - Each transport/heuristic stage assigns a stable `code` at the point the finding is authored (NOT discovered in the wild — a finite, spec-bounded set):
     - parse.ts → tx.parse_failed (§1.1)
     - content-type.ts → tx.missing_charset / tx.bad_media_type (§1.2)
     - size.ts → tx.body_too_large (§1.4)
     - encoding.ts → tx.double_encoded (and any other §1.6 codes the stage already distinguishes)
     - semantic/duplicate.ts → tx.duplicate_transfer (§1.8)
     - schema.ts info → tx.outdated_schema (§3.2, outdated:true)
   Audit every `ctx.findings.push(...)` / `record(...)` across src/ingest/stages and give each fail/info finding a stable code (pass findings do not need one — signatures only group issues). The full code list is bounded by the spec's MUST clauses — known on day one.

OUT OF SCOPE: signature computation itself (separate issue), the API response shape, any web change.

NOTE: existing finding tests + sessions/compliance tests must keep passing; update fixtures (src/ingest/fixtures/transmissions.ts) and tests to assert the new fields where they already assert on findings.
acceptance_criteria: finding table has nullable keyword/instance_path/param/code columns; repository InsertFindingInput/FindingRow + insert/insertFindings/listFindingsForSession thread them; schema.ts emits Ajv keyword+instancePath+param per error; every transport/heuristic fail/info finding carries a stable tx.* code; tests+fixtures updated and green.

title: Scale-at-volume dashboard redesign
description:
Make the dashboard usable when one or many CCEs produce hundreds — eventually thousands — of transmissions. Follow-on to the first dashboard redesign (already shipped in src/web). Source spec: design_handoff_scale_at_volume/ (README.md is the authoritative narrative; redesign/engine.js is the authoritative algorithm for signatures + trend).

The first redesign assumed a handful of transmissions. Two failures appear as volume grows: (1) detail was appended at the bottom of the transmission list, forcing a scroll past everything to read findings; (2) each requirement rendered one chip per contributing transmission (180 failures → 180 chips). Both degrade linearly with volume.

The fix shifts the unit of attention from "every transmission" to scope + exceptions + summary, via four changes:
1. Docked master–detail pane — the list scrolls in its own region; the selected transmission's detail is pinned below it and never moves the list.
2. Scoped filter bar — a time window + source selector drive scorecard, compliance summary, trend, and list together.
3. Signature (issue) summaries — each requirement summarizes failures as a few distinct deduped issues with counts + source spread, not one chip per transmission. The load-bearing idea, with real backend implications.
4. Pass-rate trend sparkline in the scorecard.

The signature model is a PURE PROJECTION of validator output — not a hand-curated catalogue. Schema errors key off Ajv's closed keyword vocabulary; transport/heuristic checks key off a stable `code` assigned where the check is authored.

ALREADY DONE (carry-over from first handoff — no issue needed): delete-all-data endpoint, outdated-schema info finding on §3.2, 7-day retention.

NOT in scope (confirmed): status/severity filters in the filter bar; a global cross-requirement "Issues" rollup; "new vs recurring since last visit".

The prototype computes everything client-side because it holds the full finding set; at true scale we compute scope/summary/signatures/trend SERVER-SIDE and paginate the list. fleet.js is prototype-only and must NOT be ported.

This epic groups the backend (structured findings, source dimension, signature engine, scope-aware summary, paginated list, api types) and frontend (sparkline/icons, filter bar, dashboard scope state, scorecard sparkline, compliance signatures, docked master-detail, virtualization) work.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard stays usable at hundreds-to-thousands of transmissions: docked master-detail (list never reflows on selection); scoped filter bar (window+source) drives scorecard/summary/trend/list together; requirements show deduped signature issues not per-tx chips; pass-rate sparkline; signatures+scope+trend computed server-side; transmission list paginated+filterable+virtualized. fleet.js NOT ported.
close_reason: All 13 children landed + reviewed. Scale-at-volume redesign complete: docked master-detail, scoped filter bar, deduped signatures (not per-tx chips), pass-rate sparkline, server-side scope/signatures/trend, paginated+filterable+virtualized list. fleet.js not ported.

title: bat.1 fixtures break the typecheck/build gate (TS2352 in cloneValid)
description: src/ingest/fixtures/transmissions.ts:62 — cloneValid() casts structuredClone(validTransmission) directly to a mutable type: `return structuredClone(validTransmission) as { meta: Record<string,unknown>; data: Record<string,unknown>[] };`. Because validTransmission is `as const` (deeply readonly), tsc rejects the cast with TS2352 ('neither type sufficiently overlaps... convert to unknown first'). `npm run build` (tsc -p tsconfig.json) fails; only `npm test` (tsx, no full typecheck) is green, which is why it slipped through. This breaks bat.1's acceptance per cdd: 'Quality gates: npm test AND the typecheck/build gate.' Fix: cast via unknown — `as unknown as { meta: ...; data: ... }` — or drop `as const` from validTransmission. Introduced by commit 0673160 (bat.1).

title: NEXT BITE: M2 ingest pipeline core (3bn.1-.7)
description:
## Underlying issues

- cce-data-delivery-validator-3bn: [epic] Ingest pipeline core (M2) — the umbrella
- 3bn.1: Ingest pipeline framework (ordered stages, short-circuit-vs-finding, status mapping, response body)
- 3bn.2: Stage 0 — session lookup (UUID exists & not expired else 404; bump last_post_at)
- 3bn.3: Stage 1 — method/TLS (POST over HTTPS via X-Forwarded-Proto; non-POST → 405)
- 3bn.4: Stages 3-5 — size (1MB wire cap → 413) / content-type (§1.2 → finding) / encoding (gzip decode + zip-bomb guard + double-encoding → 400)
- 3bn.5: Stage 6 — JSON parse (valid UTF-8 JSON else 400; persist raw_body on failure)
- 3bn.6: Stage 7 — schema validate (Ajv against meta.schemaVersion → 422 + per-error JSON-Pointer findings)
- 3bn.7: Persist transmission + findings (record EVERY POST; content_hash, wire_bytes, parse_ok/schema_ok, findings rows)

## Read first

`bd memories` is still empty — knowledge lives in the code + DESIGN.md. Read:

- `DESIGN.md` §6 (the ordered-stage table + response codes — the spec for this whole bite), §4.1 (raw-body passthrough + X-Forwarded-Proto/trustProxy contract — drives stages 1, 3-5), §8 (transmission/finding columns the persist step fills), §7 (the verifiability classes that set each finding's `severity` pass/fail/info).
- `~/.claude/projects/-home-benson-sandbox-phoenixgh-cce-data-delivery-validator/memory/architecture-decisions.md` — locked decisions (auto-memory; a spawned subagent may not inherit it).
- `docs/cce-interop-0.8.0.json` — the schema. The `transmission-metadata` object (around line 444) defines `meta.schemaVersion / transferType / transferId / transferSrc / transferredAt`; those map to the transmission columns.
- The M1 code you build ON (read before writing): `src/app.ts` (buildApp), `src/schema-registry.ts` (SchemaRegistry API), `src/db/repository.ts` (repo functions), `db/initdb/30-finding.sql` (finding columns), `src/db/repository.test.ts` (the DB-skip test idiom to copy).

## Recently-decided context

M1 landed (commits 12b61ea, c7bb739, 5a48ee8, e40acd1). Critical integration facts NOT in the issue descriptions — the executing agent MUST wire into these exact surfaces:

- **The body is NOT auto-parsed.** `src/app.ts` calls `removeAllContentTypeParsers()` + a catch-all `parseAs:'buffer'`, so `request.body` is a raw `Buffer` and `request.rawBody` holds the exact wire bytes. **Stage 6 (parse) owns JSON.parse of those bytes** — there is no Fastify JSON parser to lean on. `rawBody.length` IS the §1.4 wire-byte measurement (measured AFTER content-encoding, i.e. the bytes on the wire — do not decompress before measuring size).
- **`buildApp()` is the factory; register the ingest route there** (or in a routes module it imports). Tests drive it with `app.inject({ method, url, headers, payload })` — no port needed. The registry is already on `app.schemaRegistry` (a `SchemaRegistry`); pass it to the schema stage via closure/decorator.
- **HTTPS scheme is `request.protocol`** (Fastify honors the scoped trustProxy + `X-Forwarded-Proto`; never blanket-trusted). Stage 1 reads that for §1.1. Note HTTPS is 🔒 enforced at the Caddy edge in prod — locally the header is absent so treat a missing/non-https scheme leniently (don't 400 on it); the real job of stage 1 is **method**: non-POST → 405. To return 405 (not Fastify's default 404), register the `/i/:uuid` handler for ALL methods and let stage 1 emit 405 for non-POST.
- **Schema registry lookup:** `registry.lookup(meta.schemaVersion)` → `{ok:true, entry}` (entry has `.validate` Ajv fn + `.sha256`) or `{ok:false, requested, supported}`. Unknown version → **422** with a finding listing `supported`. On a known version, run `entry.validate(body)`; on failure emit **one finding per `entry.validate.errors[]`** with the Ajv `instancePath` as the JSON Pointer → **422**. Store `schema_version` = the normalized key (use `normalizeVersion`).
- **Persist maps meta → columns** (only when parse succeeded; null otherwise): `transfer_id`←meta.transferId, `transfer_src`←meta.transferSrc, `transfer_type`←meta.transferType, `schema_version`←normalized meta.schemaVersion, `body`←parsed JSON (jsonb, null if unparsed), `raw_body`←size-bounded original bytes (kept ESPECIALLY when parse fails, for drill-down), `content_hash`←SHA-256 of rawBody (`createHash('sha256')`), `wire_bytes`←rawBody.length, `content_type`/`content_encoding`←headers, `http_status`←the final response code, `parse_ok`/`schema_ok`←booleans. **Record EVERY POST** — `insertTransmission` already has no ON CONFLICT; do not add one.
- **Repo functions you must ADD (thin, no business logic) to `src/db/repository.ts`:** `insertFinding(s)` (finding columns: transmission_id, requirement, severity∈{pass,fail,info}, detail, pointer) and a `bumpLastPostAt(uuid)` (or fold into stage 0). `createSession`/`getSession`/`insertTransmission` already exist; all take an optional `db: Queryable` so you can pass a checked-out client. **Persist the transmission + its findings in ONE transaction** (transmission first for its id, then findings) — use `getPool().connect()` + BEGIN/COMMIT and thread the client through the repo calls.
- **No session-minting HTTP endpoint exists yet** (that's M3 / 43b.1). Tests must create sessions directly via `repository.createSession()`, then `app.inject` a POST to `/i/${session.uuid}`.
- **Persist scope:** a transmission row is recorded for any POST that reaches the body stages (has a valid session + is a POST). **404 (no session) and 405 (non-POST) return WITHOUT a transmission row** — there's no valid session_uuid FK / no delivery body to grade. Findings attach to a transmission, so they only exist once a transmission is persisted.
- **Stage numbering (avoid confusion):** DESIGN §6 numbers stages 0-8 where **stage 2 = Auth (M6, OUT OF SCOPE)** and **stage 8 = Semantic checks (M5, OUT OF SCOPE)**. M2 implements 0,1,3,4,5,6,7 + persist. Leave clean, documented insertion points (a comment / no-op slot) where stages 2 and 8 will go.
- **Success body** is a small JSON summary echoing the recorded findings count (a §6 teaching surface), e.g. `{ transmissionId, status, findings: <count> }`, returned with 200/202.

## Slicing recommendation

The stages share a `PipelineContext` and an ordered registry — so the framework agent freezes those first, then stage agents fill pre-created stub modules WITHOUT touching shared types/registry. Keep stage logic in per-stage files (e.g. `src/ingest/stages/<name>.ts`) so follow-on agents don't collide.

1. **Subagent A — 3bn.1 framework + 3bn.2 stage 0 + 3bn.3 stage 1 + 3bn.7 persist** (the vertical spine; runs first, serial).
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §6, §4.1, §8; `src/app.ts`, `src/db/repository.ts`, `db/initdb/30-finding.sql`.
   - Produces: `PipelineContext` type + `Stage`/`StageOutcome` contract (continue[+finding] vs short-circuit(status[,finding])); a `runPipeline` runner (collects findings, stops on short-circuit) with the §6 status-code mapping + success-body builder; the `POST /i/:uuid` route registered for ALL methods in/under `buildApp`; **stage 0** (session lookup → 404, bump last_post_at) and **stage 1** (method → 405, read `request.protocol`); the **terminal transactional persist** (insertTransmission + new `insertFinding(s)`, record every POST); the new repo functions. Pre-create stub modules for stages 3-5, 6, 7 (each exporting a stage that no-ops/throws "not implemented") and wire the full ordered registry so B/C only edit their own file.
   - Acceptance: `app.inject` POST to a `createSession()` uuid → persists a transmission row, returns 200 + findings-count body; POST to unknown uuid → 404, no row; GET/PUT → 405, no row. DB-touching tests skip-guarded per the repository.test.ts idiom.

2. **Subagent B — 3bn.4 (size/content-type/encoding) + 3bn.5 (JSON parse)** (after A; fills the body-bytes stub modules).
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §6 stages 3-6, §4.1; A's `PipelineContext`/`Stage` contract.
   - Produces: size stage (`rawBody.length` > 1MB → 413 + §1.4 finding); content-type stage (`application/json; charset=utf-8` check → finding, continue — 415 optional per §6); encoding stage (if `Content-Encoding: gzip` decompress with a **zip-bomb expansion guard**, detect illegal double-encoding e.g. base64 → 400 if undecodable, §1.6); parse stage (`JSON.parse(rawBody)` → 400 on failure, set `parse_ok`, ensure `raw_body` is retained for drill-down). Sets `ctx.parsedBody` on success.
   - Acceptance: unit tests via `app.inject` for each: 413 oversized, content-type finding+continue, gzip happy path, double-encoding 400, malformed-JSON 400 with raw_body persisted.

3. **Subagent C — 3bn.6 (schema validate)** (after A; fills the schema stub module; file-disjoint from B).
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §6 stage 7, §9; `src/schema-registry.ts`; the `meta` block of `docs/cce-interop-0.8.0.json`.
   - Produces: schema stage reading `ctx.parsedBody.meta.schemaVersion`, `registry.lookup(...)`; unknown version → 422 + finding listing `supported`; known version → `entry.validate(body)`, on failure one finding per Ajv error using `instancePath` as JSON Pointer → 422; set `schema_ok` + `schema_version`. A valid fixture transmission validates clean (you may craft a minimal valid 0.8.0 payload for the test).
   - Acceptance: 422 + supported-list on unknown version; 422 + per-error pointer findings on an invalid-but-parseable body; pass on a valid payload.

Run order: **A → (B ∥ C).** B and C edit disjoint stub files and do NOT touch A's frozen context/registry, so they're parallel-capable — but **commits must serialize** (concurrent commits race `git index.lock`; the implement-next coordinator already serializes). If A's `PipelineContext` turns out to be missing a field B or C needs, that's a coordination point — prefer A over-providing the context (parsedBody, normalizedSchemaVersion, meta fields, findings[]) so B/C never edit shared types.

## Out of scope

description:
## Underlying issues

- cce-data-delivery-validator-dpp: [epic] Skeleton & schema registry (M1) — the umbrella
- dpp.1: Init Node/TS project tooling (package.json, tsconfig, ESLint/Prettier, build+test scripts)
- dpp.2: Fastify server bootstrap (app factory, health endpoint, raw-body + trustProxy)
- dpp.3: docker-compose app + Postgres (healthcheck-gated bring-up)
- dpp.4: First-boot DB schema + repository layer (db/initdb ordered SQL + thin pg repo)
- dpp.5: Schema registry (vendor 0.8.0, sha256-pinned, bare-semver/$id normalize, Ajv compile at startup)

## Read first

No `bd memories` are populated yet — knowledge lives in docs, read these:

- `DESIGN.md` — the canonical spec. For this bite read: §4 + §4.1 (architecture + Caddy/trustProxy/raw-body proxy contract), §8 (data model — exact session/transmission/finding columns + indexes), §9 (schema registry: never-fetch-at-runtime, normalized matching, content-hash "blessed bytes", Ajv compile-once), §13 (tech stack), §14.1 (build order — M1 is item 1).
- `~/.claude/projects/-home-benson-sandbox-phoenixgh-cce-data-delivery-validator/memory/architecture-decisions.md` — locked decisions (auto-memory; a spawned subagent may not inherit it, so read explicitly).
- Sibling repo `../tremble/db/initdb/*.sql` — the ordered-SQL convention to mirror. `10-source-artifact.sql` is the direct ancestor of our `transmission` table (content_hash/byte_size/content_type/received_at). **Key divergence: tremble makes `content_hash` UNIQUE to dedup-and-drop; we must NOT — `content_hash` is non-unique here because duplicate detection is the §1.8 signal we grade.**
- `docs/cce-interop-0.8.0.json` — the draft-07 schema to vendor into the registry (dpp.5). Keep byte-identical to published; do NOT patch the stale `0.1.1` example (tracked separately as cce-data-delivery-validator-ven).

## Recently-decided context

Not yet written into the underlying issue descriptions:

- **`tremble` lives at `../tremble`** (sibling dir, vanilla Postgres+PostGIS). Lift its `db/initdb/` ordered-SQL bring-up and `source_artifact` content-addressed pattern. Do not import pg_duckdb / Parquet paths — those are tremble's deferred cold-storage, irrelevant here.
- **M1 is skeleton ONLY.** Success = `docker-compose up` brings up Postgres (healthcheck-gated) then the app; the app boots, serves a health endpoint, applies the DB schema on first boot, and compiles the 0.8.0 schema with Ajv at startup. NO ingest logic, NO request validation pipeline, NO endpoints beyond health in this bite.
- **Raw-body access is a hard requirement** (dpp.2): the app must measure the exact wire bytes of POST bodies for §1.4, so configure Fastify to retain/access the raw body (e.g. a content-type parser that keeps the Buffer) — don't let a JSON body parser discard it. Not exercised until M2, but the bootstrap must not preclude it.
- **trustProxy scoped to Caddy only** (dpp.2): Fastify `trustProxy` must trust the proxy address, not blanket-trust, so `X-Forwarded-Proto` (how §1.1 HTTPS is known) can't be spoofed by clients. App port is never publicly exposed.
- **Schema registry is a lookup table, never a fetcher** (dpp.5): `meta.schemaVersion` is an opaque key. Normalize on ingest — accept bare semver (`0.8.0`) OR a full `$id` URL, extract MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, exact-match lookup, no fuzzy fallback. Unknown version → 422 listing supported versions. Pin each version by sha256 of canonical bytes; expose the hash for the dashboard's "validated against official 0.8.0 (sha256 …)" claim. (The 422 wiring lands fully in M2; M1 just needs the registry loaded + compiled + the lookup/normalize API present.)
- **DB schema applied as ordered SQL on first boot** (dpp.4), mirroring tremble — NOT a migration runner (deferred). Columns/indexes are spelled out verbatim in DESIGN.md §8; follow them exactly (esp. `content_hash bytea` non-unique, the two duplicate-detection indexes, `body jsonb` nullable).

## Slicing recommendation

`package.json` is the shared coordination point — naive full parallelism causes dependency-merge conflicts. Slice to keep package.json edits non-overlapping:

1. **Subagent A — dpp.1 (tooling foundation).** Serial, runs first; everything depends on it.
   - Produces: `package.json` (scripts: build/test/lint/dev), `tsconfig.json`, ESLint+Prettier config, `src/` skeleton dir, a trivial test that runs green.
   - Acceptance: `npm install && npm run build && npm test && npm run lint` all pass on an empty skeleton.

2. **Subagent B — dpp.2 + dpp.5 combined (server + registry).** After A. Combined because both add runtime deps to package.json (fastify; ajv) AND the registry compiles at server startup, so they share the app-factory wiring.
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §4.1, §9, §13; `docs/cce-interop-0.8.0.json`.
   - Produces: Fastify app factory + health endpoint + raw-body/trustProxy config; schema-registry module (vendor 0.8.0, sha256 pin, normalize, Ajv compile-at-startup, lookup API) wired so startup fails loudly if the blessed bytes don't compile.
   - Acceptance: app boots; `GET /health` 200; startup logs "registry: 0.8.0 (sha256 …) compiled"; unit test covers semver/$id normalization + unknown-version path.

3. **Subagent C — dpp.3 (docker-compose).** Can run in PARALLEL with B — touches `docker-compose.yml` + `Dockerfile` + `.dockerignore`, not `src/` or package.json deps.
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §4, §13; `../tremble`'s compose for the healthcheck-gated pattern.
   - Produces: compose with Postgres (healthcheck) + app service that waits on db healthy; Dockerfile building the TS app.
   - Acceptance: `docker-compose up` brings up Postgres healthy then the app; health endpoint reachable through the mapped port.

4. **Subagent D — dpp.4 (DB schema + repo).** After C (needs the Postgres container/compose) and after package.json settles (adds `pg`). 
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §8; `../tremble/db/initdb/10-source-artifact.sql` and indexes file.
   - Produces: `db/initdb/*.sql` (ordered) creating session/transmission/finding tables + indexes per §8; thin `pg` repository layer.
   - Acceptance: fresh `docker-compose up` applies the SQL on first boot; a repo-layer smoke test inserts+reads a session row.

Run order: **A → (B ∥ C) → D.** B and C share no files and run in parallel. D follows C. If running B and D's package.json edits risk colliding, serialize the `npm install` step: let B land first, then D rebases its `pg` add onto B's package.json.

## Out of scope

Do NOT touch in this bite (these are M2+ and have their own issues):

- The ingest pipeline / `POST /i/{uuid}` and any of stages 0–8 (epic 3bn.*). M1 only needs the registry *loadable*, not *invoked* on requests.
- Sessions API / `POST /api/sessions` / dashboard read API (epic 43b.*).
- Web UI (epic yih.*), §1.3 auth (epic ct4.*), semantic checks (epic 8ji.*), retention worker (yhg.*).
- Caddy config itself — that's the deploy edge; M1 only honors the contract assumptions (trustProxy, raw body) inside the app.
- Patching cosmetic schema issues in the vendored 0.8.0 (stale example, $id phrasing) — keep bytes identical; standard-revision proposals are tracked in cce-data-delivery-validator-ven.

## Commit + test expectations

- Commit to this repo when each piece is tested and green. **Do not push** (no git remote configured anyway; local-only).
- Match the terse `prefix: subject` commit style (`git log --oneline` first; recent: `design: lock schema versioning…`, `beads: implementation issue graph…`). Suggested prefixes: `skeleton:`, `db:`, `registry:`.
- Quality gates before each commit: `npm run build && npm test && npm run lint` green; for dpp.3/dpp.4, a clean `docker-compose up` from scratch.
- Close each underlying issue (`bd close dpp.N`) as it lands; close the epic `dpp` when all five are done.

title: README overstates §4 as entirely active-only (🔌); 4.6-4.9 are self-attestation
description:
README.md:186 ("Status and v1 scope", added in 62eb9ae) states:

> **No active conformance harness** — nothing deliberately returns 429/503/5xx to measure a supplier's retry count, backoff shape, or `Retry-After` handling. That is why **the whole of §4 sits in the 🔌 column.**

This is wrong. Per DESIGN.md §7 and src/api/compliance-matrix.ts:139-160, only 4.1-4.5 are active-only. 4.6 (log failed attempts), 4.7 (email + SLA), 4.8 (monitor transmission status) and 4.9 (notify on elevated failures) are classed `attestation` (📝) — 'supplier-internal', i.e. NOT provable from the receiving side at all, ever. 4.4 is dual 🔌/📝.

Why it matters: this sits in the honesty proposition, which dkz.2 calls the product's distinguishing idea. A ministry or PQS reader is told that all nine §4 requirements are merely *deferred* pending an active harness, when four of them are permanently outside what any receiver can establish. That misrepresents the one claim the README is asking the reader to trust.

It also contradicts the README's own count table 120 lines earlier (README.md:60), which gives 🔌 = 8 rows total. If all of §4 were 🔌 that would be 9 in §4 alone, plus 5.1-5.3 = 12.

Fix: scope the claim to the rows it actually covers, e.g. '...which is why §4.1-4.5 sit in the 🔌 column; §4.6-4.9 are supplier-internal and stay 📝.'

Not filed as P1: dkz.2's acceptance (what/why/who/how-to-run/where-hosted) is still met, and the correct per-class counts are stated accurately elsewhere in the same file.

title: DESIGN.md §8 claims an over-cap/undecodable gzip body 'never reaches the insert' — a row IS persisted
description:
fbd22ce rewrote DESIGN.md §8 to state the implemented reality of raw_body bounding (399 acceptance: "§8 must state implemented reality"). One clause in that new paragraph is false.

DESIGN.md:239-240 (§8, "On raw_body size"):

  "**gzip `maxOutputLength` — 1 MiB.** The zip-bomb guard: a gzip body whose
   output would exceed it throws and is rejected `400` as undecodable, so it
   never reaches the insert either."

Read in parallel with the preceding bullet ("Beyond 2 MiB, Fastifys generic 413 fires and nothing is recorded"), this tells the reader that an over-cap or otherwise undecodable gzip body leaves no stored row. It does.

The encoding stage is a BODY stage, i.e. downstream of the persistence boundary:
- src/ingest/stages/encoding.ts:76-88 — gunzipSync({maxOutputLength: 1_048_576}) throws; the catch records a 1.6 fail finding and returns halt(400).
- src/ingest/route.ts:239-243 — "Body stages (3-7[, 8]): reached with a valid session + POST, so a row is persisted regardless of whether a body stage short-circuits." persistTransmission() is called unconditionally on the post-body path.
- src/ingest/route.ts:141-145,183 — storedRawBody() falls back to ctx.rawBody when nothing was decoded, so raw_body holds the still-compressed wire bytes read as UTF-8 (invalid sequences -> U+FFFD) with NUL stripped.

So the sentence is wrong twice over: a row IS inserted, and its raw_body is NOT bounded by the 1 MiB gzip ceiling — it is the up-to-2 MiB compressed body, which U+FFFD substitution can EXPAND (3 bytes per invalid byte) to several MiB of text. The codebase already knows this: src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx:566-576 documents the "copy longer than wire -> undecodable bytes were substituted" case explicitly.

This is not the open cap-vs-no-cap decision (1z9) and does not ask for one: it asks that the honesty paragraph stop asserting a persistence outcome the code does not have. Suggested correction: say that an undecodable/over-cap gzip body still persists a row whose raw_body is the raw compressed bytes rendered as UTF-8, so the 1 MiB gzip ceiling bounds only the DECODED path.
acceptance_criteria: DESIGN.md §8 describes the undecodable/over-cap gzip path as it is implemented: halt(400) at stage 5 still persists a transmission row (route.ts:239-243), and raw_body on that path is the compressed wire bytes, not a 1 MiB-bounded decoded payload.

title: hasCustomDataSchema() accepts {} and ['']: an empty declaration passes §3.1
description:
src/ingest/stages/semantic/custom-schema.ts:180-188 (hasCustomDataSchema). Its own docstring states the contract: "Present means: the key exists with a value that actually carries a declaration ... `null`, `` and `[]` are treated as absent: they name no schema, so they cannot discharge the obligation."

Two values name no schema yet return true:
  - `meta.customDataSchema: {}` — isPlainObject({}) is true, so the final `return isPlainObject(value)` passes it. Per published 0.8.2 `$defs/custom-data-schema-item`, the inline form REQUIRES `$id` (`"required": ["$id"]`), so `{}` is not a declaration by the spec that introduced the field.
  - `meta.customDataSchema: [""]` / `[{}]` — only `length > 0` is checked, never the items.

Effect: a payload carrying undeclared z-prefixed custom objects gets §3.1 PASS instead of the FAIL 5bs.1 exists to produce, and 0.8.1 (the only registered schema version) has additionalProperties:true throughout, so nothing else catches it. This is a false PASS in a conformance grader.

src/ingest/stages/semantic/custom-schema.test.ts:325-335 covers "", [] and null but not {} or [""].

Suggested fix: treat {} as absent (or require a non-empty $id / at least one non-empty item) and extend the empty-forms test loop.
acceptance_criteria: meta.customDataSchema values that carry no actual declaration ({}, [""], [{}]) are treated as absent and produce the §3.1 fail; unit tests cover them alongside the existing "", [] and null cases.

title: Raw-payload note claims 'Shown decoded' for encodings that were never decoded
description:
src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx:584 (describeStoredCopy, commit fffae12, bite 72k/5bs.3).

  const decoded = encoding !== null && encoding !== '' && encoding.toLowerCase() !== 'identity';

This treats ANY non-empty, non-identity Content-Encoding as proof the stored copy was decoded. It was not. src/ingest/route.ts storedRawBody() stores getDecodedBody(ctx) ?? ctx.rawBody, and src/ingest/stages/encoding.ts only calls setDecodedBody() on the ONE success path (single-layer gzip that gunzips). Every other path halts 400 BEFORE decoding:
  - unsupported token (br, deflate, base64, ...) -> tx.unsupported_encoding
  - gzip that fails to gunzip / exceeds maxOutputLength -> tx.undecodable_body
  - gzip-of-gzip -> tx.double_encoded

src/ingest/route.ts persists a row for every body-stage halt ('a row is persisted regardless of whether a body stage short-circuits'), so these rows reach the dashboard with content_encoding set, body NULL, and raw_body = the RAW wire bytes run through toString('utf8') (invalid sequences -> U+FFFD) with NUL stripped.

The inspector then renders that mojibake under the note at line 591:
  'Shown decoded: N bytes of payload from M gzip bytes on the wire.'
with warn:false. That is affirmatively false — nothing was decoded — and it suppresses the UTF-8-substitution disclosure the same function emits on the identity path ('Altered: ... undecodable bytes were substituted').

Breaks 5bs.3's requirement to 'say so in the UI rather than implying the user is seeing everything', in exactly the parse-failure case the inspector exists for (DESIGN §8). The §1.6 fail finding and the amber compression cell are on screen saying the encoding was rejected while this note says the payload decoded cleanly.

Fix direction: gate the decoded branch on evidence of an actual decode rather than on the header alone — e.g. only when content_encoding is gzip AND there is no §1.6 fail finding (tx.unsupported_encoding / tx.undecodable_body / tx.double_encoded) on the transmission; otherwise fall through to the wire-size comparison so the >wire case reports substitution honestly.

title: raw_body 'size-bounded' claim is documented but not implemented
description: db/initdb/20-transmission.sql, src/db/repository.ts, and DESIGN.md §8 all describe the stored raw_body drill-down copy as size-bounded, but storedRawBody() in src/ingest/route.ts only gzip-decodes and strips NUL — insertTransmission never slices, and the column is unbounded text. The only real ceilings are Fastify's 2MiB bodyLimit (no row written at all beyond it) and gzip maxOutputLength 1MiB (throws → 400). Found during 72k/5bs.3 (commit fffae12): the new inspector's truncation disclosure had to be written against wire_bytes comparison because no write-side cap exists to quote. Fix is a decision: either implement the write-side cap (and pick the bound) or correct the comments/DESIGN §8. The UI's truncation branch already handles a future cap correctly.
notes:
Exact ceilings confirmed during 399 (fbd22ce): DEFAULT_BODY_LIMIT=2MiB (src/app.ts:66), MAX_DECODED_BYTES=1,048,576 (encoding.ts:37), MAX_WIRE_BYTES=1,048,576 (size.ts:14); no write-side slice anywhere. DESIGN §8 now states implemented reality and references this issue. The stale 'size-bounded' claim SURVIVES in: db/initdb/20-transmission.sql (header line ~13, column comment ~48-49, COMMENT ON COLUMN ~62-63) and src/db/repository.ts:80 — fixing those is part of this issue's resolution, whichever way the cap decision goes.
ESCALATED to human queue 2026-08-01. Options: (A) implement a write-side cap on the stored raw_body drill-down copy — recommendation 1 MiB to match MAX_WIRE_BYTES/MAX_DECODED_BYTES, making the documented 'size-bounded' intent true and bounding storage; UI truncation branch (fffae12/9f08a60) already handles a cap correctly; also fix the stale comments listed in the earlier note. (B) decide no-cap and correct the remaining comments (route.ts:129, 20-transmission.sql) to match. RECOMMENDATION: (A), 1 MiB.
DECIDED by Benson 2026-08-02: option (B) variant — do NOT implement a write-side cap. Accept the body and flag the failure via findings. Note the current pipeline already does the accept-and-flag part for 1–2MiB bodies: sizeStage() is AFTER the persistence boundary, so an oversize body persists a row with a §1.4 fail finding and returns 413. Remaining work: remove the stale 'size-bounded' claims — db/initdb/20-transmission.sql (header ~13, column comment ~48-49, COMMENT ON COLUMN ~62-63), src/db/repository.ts:80, and the storedRawBody() docblock in src/ingest/route.ts (~129) — so docs match no-cap reality. Residual ceiling left as-is unless Benson says otherwise: Fastify DEFAULT_BODY_LIMIT=2MiB still rejects >2MiB with 413 and NO row (accept-and-flag does not extend past it), and gzip MAX_DECODED_BYTES=1MiB still 400s.

title: §1.3 guidance tells suppliers to pick an auth method, but the Setup panel offers no choice
description:
src/web/components/requirementReference.ts (entry '1.3', guidance) — introduced by 81f0b05 — now reads:

  'Auth is opt-in: enable it from the endpoint panel, pick the header-token or HTTP Basic method, and we generate a credential for you.'

The 'pick the header-token or HTTP Basic method' clause is not true of the shipped UI. src/web/components/Setup.tsx:141 is the only enable path and calls:

  const result = await enableAuth(session.uuid);

with no body. src/web/api.ts:380-383 defaults body to {}, and Setup.tsx:140 comments 'Empty body -> service defaults to the header method (zero-config opt-in).' There is no radio/select/method control anywhere in Setup.tsx — auth_method is only ever READ back for display (Setup.tsx:166, 294). A supplier who wants HTTP Basic cannot get it from the endpoint panel; only a direct POST /api/sessions/:uuid/auth with an explicit method reaches the 'basic' branch.

This is a regression introduced by the commit: the prior guidance said only 'enable it from the endpoint panel and we generate a credential for you', which was accurate. The text field for 1.3 is correct and faithful to the PDF; the defect is in guidance only.

This violates the file's own header discipline (src/web/components/requirementReference.ts:14-22): guidance is the 'GENERAL how-we-check-it explanation' and the documented failure mode of the prototype was guidance asserting things that were not true of the running service. The guidance is user-visible — ComplianceCard.tsx:349 renders it in the drill-down.

Fix is either (a) drop the 'pick the ... method' clause and say the panel issues a header token, or (b) add the method choice to the panel. Note cce-data-delivery-validator-5bs.4 (Bearer, RFC 6750) already requires the 1.3 opt-in UI to 'offer Bearer as a third choice' — if 5bs.4 lands the picker, option (b) subsumes this and the guidance becomes true. Does NOT affect 5bs.5's acceptance: all 27 text fields verify verbatim against the 2025 PDF.

title: Outdated-but-valid schema version renders section 3.2 as "untested"
description:
A transmission that validates successfully against a registered but OLDER schema version is recorded as severity=info with outdated=true (src/ingest/stages/schema.ts). deriveStatus() in src/api/compliance-matrix.ts only counts pass and fail:

  if (counts.pass === 0 && counts.fail === 0) return "untested";

So a session whose traffic all used an older version shows section 3.2 as UNTESTED — despite every payload having been validated and having passed. That is not honest: "untested" claims we did not check, when we did check and it succeeded against an older schema.

info-not-pass was a deliberate decision (see bd memory schema-registry-0.8.1-current-outdated). The consequence for the derived row status was almost certainly not intended.

Options:
  (a) Add a fourth severity `warn`. Requires a NEW numbered DDL file to widen the CHECK on finding.severity (pass|fail|info), plus a new DisplayStatus and dashboard treatment. Most expressive, most invasive.
  (b) Keep severity=info and add a distinct DisplayStatus (e.g. `pass-outdated`) derived from the existing outdated flag, which is already threaded through repository -> sessions -> FindingView and already drives the amber OUTDATED SCHEMA tag. Cheapest path that removes the lie.
  (c) Count it as pass and let the existing amber tag carry the warning. Simplest, weakest signal.

RECOMMENDATION: warn, not fail.

IMPORTANT CHANGE OF CIRCUMSTANCE (2026-07-31): the earlier fairness argument against FAIL was that 0.8.1 had never been published, so failing a supplier for not using it was indefensible. **0.8.1 was published upstream on 2026-07-30**, and 0.8.2 now exists too. That argument is weaker now. It has NOT disappeared: suppliers need a transition window after any publication, and a supplier pinned to a version that was current when they integrated has not done anything wrong. A warning that names the current version and the one they used is still the right verdict; revisit FAIL only if a deprecation policy with dates is ever defined.

Depends on the P0 registry fix landing first, since which versions count as "current" vs "outdated" changes once 0.8.1/0.8.2 register.
acceptance_criteria: A session using only an older-but-valid schema version no longer displays as untested; the dashboard distinguishes validated-against-current from validated-against-outdated; the chosen severity model is recorded.
notes:
ESCALATED to human queue 2026-08-01. The issue body carries the full option analysis (a: new warn severity + DDL; b: pass-outdated DisplayStatus from the existing outdated flag; c: count as pass with amber tag) and RECOMMENDATION: warn-not-fail semantics. Loop's added recommendation: option (b) — cheapest path that removes the 'untested' lie, no DDL, the outdated flag is already threaded through to the UI. Decide together with fvw (registration creates the first real outdated cohort).
DECIDED by Benson 2026-08-02: LOCKED on option (b) — keep severity=info and derive a distinct DisplayStatus (e.g. pass-outdated) from the existing outdated flag, which is already threaded repository -> sessions -> FindingView and drives the amber OUTDATED SCHEMA tag. No new severity, no DDL. Context from fvw's resolution: 0.8.2/0.8.3 are IGNORED until instructed, so 0.8.1 stays the only registered (and therefore current) version — the outdated path stays theoretical until an older version ever registers alongside a newer one, but the 'untested' lie in deriveStatus() should still be fixed now.
close_reason: dd999b8 pass-outdated DisplayStatus (option b): fail dominates, outdated no longer renders untested, amber treatment reuses --mixed family; +8 tests

title: Add CI; skipped Postgres tests currently read as green
description:
There is no CI configuration of any kind (no .github/, no other pipeline config), and the test suite understates its own coverage gap.

Observed on a clean run: "# tests 217 / # pass 178 / # fail 0 / # skipped 39". The 39 skips are Postgres-gated - src/db/repository.test.ts:34 probes the DB once and sets skip = "no Postgres reachable (DATABASE_URL/PG* unset or DB down)" for the whole suite, and the ingest/api suites do the same. So npm test with no database prints fail 0 and looks fully green while the entire persistence and ingest-integration layer never executed.

A first-time contributor will reasonably conclude the DB layer is covered. It is not, unless they happened to run docker compose up -d postgres first.

Wanted:
  1. A CI workflow that stands up Postgres (service container or docker compose), runs the full suite, and runs npm run lint and npm run build.
  2. CI fails, or at minimum warns loudly, if any test skips - a skip in CI means the DB gating silently broke.
  3. Make the local story obvious: either a test script that brings up Postgres, or a clear README note that npm test without a database exercises only the pure-logic subset.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs tests against a real Postgres plus lint and build; skipped tests do not pass silently in CI; the local no-database behaviour is documented.
