title: Write an HTTP API reference
description:
The HTTP surface is documented nowhere outside source code. A supplier integrating server-side, rather than clicking through the dashboard, has nothing to read.

Routes actually registered (verified 2026-07-27):
  - POST /i/:uuid                    src/ingest/route.ts (registered for all methods so non-POST returns 405)
  - POST /api/sessions               src/api/sessions.ts:200
  - POST /api/sessions/... (second)  src/api/sessions.ts:218
  - DELETE (two routes)              src/api/sessions.ts:270, :292
  - GET (two routes)                 src/api/sessions.ts:320, :436
  - GET /health                      src/app.ts:141

For each: path, method, auth expectations, request shape, response shape, and status codes. The ingest endpoint especially needs the full status-code table from DESIGN.md section 6 (404 unknown session, 405 non-POST, 401 auth, 413 oversize, 400 undecodable/unparseable, 422 schema failure, 2xx accepted), since the response code IS part of what the tool teaches.

The DELETE routes deserve particular care: they destroy a session and its data, and possession of the UUID is the only authorization. That needs to be stated plainly.

Cross-reference the section 7 verifiability matrix so integrators understand which findings are graded versus informational.
acceptance_criteria: A public API reference covers every registered route with request/response shapes and status codes, including the ingest status-code table and the destructive DELETE semantics.

title: Document schema version publication status and the identifier-vs-locator point
description:
The schema registry treats 0.8.1 as the current version, and src/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.1.json carries $id https://schemas.2to8.cc/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.1.json. Per the workspace CLAUDE.md, 0.8.1 exists in four repos but was NEVER published to that URL.

So the $id of our current schema dereferences to a 404. This is harmless to the validator by design - DESIGN.md section 9 is emphatic that schemaVersion is a lookup key and schemas are never fetched at runtime - but it will absolutely generate confused questions from suppliers who try to open the URL, and it undercuts the "validated against the official 0.8.x" claim the dashboard makes.

Needs an explicit, honest note wherever schema versions are surfaced (README, DESIGN.md section 9, and ideally the dashboard provenance line): which versions are vendored, which is current, which are published upstream, and the reminder that $id is an identifier and not a locator.

Related: cce-data-delivery-validator-ven (standard-revision proposals) already proposes mechanically linking $id and schemaVersion and publishing a content-hash manifest upstream - this issue is the interim disclosure, not the fix.
acceptance_criteria: The publication status of each vendored schema version is stated where users will see it, and the identifier-not-locator point is made explicitly.
notes:
SUPERSEDED PREMISE 2026-07-31: 0.8.1 WAS published upstream on 2026-07-30, so the original framing ("current schema is not published, its $id 404s") no longer holds. 0.8.2 also now exists in the authoring folder. What survives and is still worth documenting: (a) which vendored versions are registered, which is current, and which are published; (b) that $id is an identifier and NOT a locator, and the validator never dereferences it at runtime (DESIGN section 9). Also note the republished 0.8.1 changed dialect to JSON Schema 2020-12 and fixed the stale 0.1.1 schemaVersion example - see the P0 cce-data-delivery-validator-2hg.
PUBLICATION STATUS MEASURED 2026-07-31 against https://docs.2to8.cc/cce-data-interop/schemas/cce-interop-<version>.json:
  0.8.0  HTTP 200  sha256 e6614cc7...  (published)
  0.8.1  HTTP 200  sha256 290290fd...  (published; what we vendor + register)
  0.8.2  HTTP 200  sha256 b6ee10cf...  (PUBLISHED - see note below)
  0.8.3  HTTP 404                       (authoring folder only, not published)

CONCRETE $id DEFECT WORTH DOCUMENTING: every published schema declares
  "$id": "https://schemas.2to8.cc/schemas/cce-interop-<version>.json"
but that host DOES NOT RESOLVE (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). The artifact actually lives on a different host AND a different path. So the $id is a dangling identifier: any supplier who treats it as a locator and dereferences it gets a DNS failure, not a schema.

This is the strongest possible concrete argument for DESIGN section 9 (never fetch at runtime; $id is an identifier, not a locator) and for proposals 1-4 in cce-data-delivery-validator-ven. It should be reported upstream and stated plainly in whatever supplier-facing docs come out of this issue.

Our normalizeVersion() handles BOTH URL forms (it extracts the semver triple from any string), verified for the docs.2to8.cc form, the schemas.2to8.cc $id form, and the bare semver - so a supplier copying either URL into meta.schemaVersion resolves correctly. No code change needed; a test case pinning the real publication URL form would be a cheap guard.
$id DECISION (2026-07-31): the $id will change to a URN upstream, and no-runtime-fetch is confirmed as the right model. Verified normalizeVersion() already resolves URN forms carrying a semver triple (urn:2to8:schemas:cce-interop:0.8.1 -> 0.8.1, and longer urn:iso:std:... forms too); a URN with a non-semver version returns null and correctly falls through to the 422 unsupported path. So the upstream $id change needs NO code here. Worth adding a test pinning both the URN form and the real docs.2to8.cc publication URL, since those are what suppliers will copy.

title: Dashboard flashes full-screen Loading on every scope/filter change
description: src/web/routes/Dashboard.tsx:124-172. The initial-load effect (deps [load]) unconditionally calls setState({phase:'loading'}) before load(). Post-4h4.9, load() now closes over scope state and lists window/source/failuresOnly/selectedSignature in its useCallback deps (line 162), so load is recreated on any filter change, re-firing the [load] effect (line 165-172) and blanking the ENTIRE dashboard (header, scorecard, FilterBar, both panes) to the 'Loading…' screen until the summary read returns. Pre-commit load depended only on [uuid], so this effect fired only on mount/uuid change. Acceptance asks that changing window/source 'recomputes everything above the list and refetches the list' in place; instead the user loses the FilterBar (and their just-made selection control) for a network round-trip on every toggle. The 5s poll path is unaffected (uses background mode, no loading reset). Fix: drive the loading reset on uuid only, or guard the loading-phase reset behind a not-yet-ready check / fetch-in-scope via a non-load-keyed effect, so scope changes refetch without dropping the ready render.

title: NEXT BITE: paginated filterable transmission list endpoint (4h4.5)
description:
## Underlying issues

- cce-data-delivery-validator-4h4.5 (P2): Add GET /api/sessions/:uuid/transmissions — a paginated, filterable transmission-list endpoint (window+source+failuresOnly+signatureKey, reverse-chron, cursor/offset paging) + a repository query. All deps (4h4.1 structured findings, 4h4.2 source, 4h4.3 signatures) are CLOSED.

## Read first

Memories to query:
- `bd memories schema` → schema-registry-0.8.1-current-outdated — outdated §3.2 info finding (severity=info, outdated=true); isIssue() counts it, so a signatureKey for an outdated-schema signature must match those tx via txMatchesSig.
- `bd memories retention` → retention-window-7days — per-session volume is bounded by the 7-day retention window; relevant to the "what scales" trade-off below.

Documents:
- 4h4.5 own description — canonical contract (params, response shape, the SQL-vs-post-filter decision it poses). DO NOT restate; this bite is execution-only.
- src/api/scope.ts — REUSE parseWindow/parseSource (param parsing with default-fallback, no 400) + inScope/scopeTransmissions + the Window type. NOTE: the window→ms map (WINDOW_MS) is currently PRIVATE; the SQL time-bound needs it.
- src/api/signatures.ts — REUSE txMatchesSig(tx, key) / isIssue / sigKey for the signatureKey cross-filter (consume; do NOT edit). It is the single source of truth for signature membership.
- src/api/source.ts — deriveSourceView: source key = TRIMMED transfer_src, null/blank → "" (UNKNOWN_SOURCE_KEY). This normalization is why a naive SQL `transfer_src = $source` is WRONG for the source filter (see below).
- src/db/repository.ts — listTransmissions (~255, the `(session_uuid, received_at DESC)` index + TransmissionRow shape) and listFindingsForSession (~279). Model the new query on these.
- src/api/sessions.ts — the 4h4.4 scope-aware GET handler (~184-322) just landed; mirror its param-parsing + view-building (deriveSourceView, toFindingView) for consistency.

## Recently-decided context

Facts established THIS session (4h4.4 landed at ac22588) that shape 4h4.5:

1. **scope.ts is the shared scope core — reuse it, do not re-derive.** parseWindow/parseSource already give resilient param parsing (unknown → default, never 400). For the SUMMARY endpoint scope.ts filters an in-memory array (scopeTransmissions). The LIST endpoint should instead push the window time-bound + cursor into SQL for scale. To keep the window math single-source, EXPORT a tiny helper from scope.ts — e.g. `windowLowerBound(window: Window, now: number): number | null` (null for "all") — and use it both to build the SQL `received_at >= $lo` bound here AND (optionally refactor) in the summary. Small, same-module addition; add a unit test.

2. **Two filters do NOT map cleanly to a single SQL column — this is the crux of the issue trade-off:**
   - `source`: the key is the TRIMMED transfer_src with null/blank collapsed to "" (deriveSourceView). `WHERE transfer_src = $source` misses the unknown bucket and ignores trimming. Either normalize in SQL (trim + null/blank → "") to match deriveSourceView EXACTLY, or derive+filter in app.
   - `signatureKey`: membership is txMatchesSig = "tx has a finding where isIssue && sigKey===key". sigKey concatenates req|keyword|generalizedPath|param (array indices stripped via /\d+/→/*) OR req|code OR req|detail. Reconstructing this in SQL duplicates signatures.ts sigKey and risks DRIFT — the signature memory is explicit that membership keys off the structured fields via the shared engine. Prefer reusing txMatchesSig in app to avoid two sources of truth.

3. **Recommended approach (the issue says "pick what scales + document"):** Per-session volume is BOUNDED by 7-day retention (one client's deliveries — thousands at most, not millions), so an app-side filter over a window-scoped candidate set is acceptable AND keeps source/signatureKey correctness single-source: push the `window` time-bound + reverse-chron ORDER into SQL (reuse the received_at DESC index), fetch the windowed candidates + their findings, then apply source (deriveSourceView) + failuresOnly + signatureKey (txMatchesSig) + cursor pagination in app. Document the trade-off in a comment: pure-SQL paginate is faster but forces a fragile SQL re-impl of sigKey/source-normalization; app-filter trades that for a bounded per-session scan. If the implementer instead pushes everything to SQL, the source-normalization + sigKey-reconstruction MUST mirror source.ts/signatures.ts exactly and carry a test pinning the equivalence.

4. **Cursor over offset** (issue prefers it): a stable reverse-chron cursor on (received_at DESC, id DESC). Page-size param with a sane default + hard cap. Return next-cursor + hasMore.

## Slicing recommendation

1. **Single subagent — list endpoint + repository query (4h4.5)**
   - Reads: the files above. Edits: src/db/repository.ts (new filtered/paginated query) + src/api/sessions.ts (new GET /api/sessions/:uuid/transmissions handler) + src/api/scope.ts (export windowLowerBound + test).

Repository query reuses the (session_uuid, received_at DESC) index and is documented.
   - Acceptance: matches 4h4.5 acceptance — all four filters + pagination(cursor+limit cap); signatureKey membership EQUALS txMatchesSig/sigKey (test it against signatures.ts on a fixture, not a re-impl); reverse-chron stable ordering; unknown window/source fall back to defaults; repository query added + trade-off documented.
   - Gates before commit: npm test, npm run typecheck:web, tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit, npm run lint.

Run order: serial, ONE agent. Shares src/api/sessions.ts + src/api/scope.ts with already-landed 4h4.4 work (sequential, not parallel — no other bite touches these concurrently).

## Out of scope

- Client work: row virtualization (4h4.13) and the list/detail UI rendering. Server only.
- The typed web api client (4h4.6) — separate bite.
- Editing src/api/signatures.ts (done, aa3ed03) — consume txMatchesSig/sigKey; if a real defect, file a bd issue.
- Changing the 4h4.4 summary response shape — only ADD windowLowerBound to scope.ts; do not alter the summary contract. Leave the existing client working.

title: Paginated, filterable transmission list endpoint
description:
Add a paginated, filterable transmission-list endpoint so the client holds a window of rows, not all of them. At true thousands the list region cannot ship every row in the session read.

WHY: Header reads "Transmissions · showing {visible} of {scoped}". The list applies scope + Failures-only + active-signature cross-filter, reverse-chron, and must paginate.

WHAT (src/api/sessions.ts + repository.ts):

1. Endpoint (e.g. GET /api/sessions/:uuid/transmissions) accepting query params:
   - `window` (15m|1h|6h|all) and `source` (key|all) — same scope semantics as the scope-aware summary.
   - `failuresOnly` (bool) — keep only transmissions with ≥1 fail finding.
   - `signatureKey` (string) — keep only transmissions matching that signature (txMatchesSig from the signature engine: tx has a finding where isIssue && sigKey===key). The cross-filter from a clicked signature row.
   - pagination: cursor OR offset (choose one; cursor on received_at+id is preferred for a reverse-chron stable list). Page size param with a sane default/cap.

2. Response: a page of transmission rows (the existing TransmissionView shape + source/sourceCode/sourceLabel + each row's findings for the docked detail; or fetch findings lazily per selection — decide and document) PLUS the scoped total (the "of {total}" denominator, AFTER scope+failuresOnly+signature filters as appropriate — match what the header means) and a next-cursor/hasMore.

3. repository.ts: add a filtered+paginated query. The signatureKey filter needs structured finding fields; implement membership either in SQL (join finding, reconstruct the key) or by post-filtering a candidate set — pick the approach that scales and document the trade-off. Reuse the (session_uuid, received_at DESC) index for ordering.

4. Keep the per-tx findings available for the docked detail (the detail pane renders StatusPill + §req links + OUTDATED SCHEMA tag + detail + pointer + object inventory). If findings are not inlined per row, provide the path the detail pane uses.

DEPENDS ON: structured findings, signature engine (txMatchesSig / sigKey), source dimension.
OUT OF SCOPE: row virtualization in the client (separate issue, pairs with this) and the list/detail UI.
acceptance_criteria: GET list endpoint accepts window+source+failuresOnly+signatureKey+pagination(cursor/offset+limit cap); returns a page of tx rows (with source fields + findings access for the docked detail), the scoped total denominator, and next-cursor/hasMore; signatureKey membership matches txMatchesSig/sigKey; reverse-chron stable ordering; repository query added + documented.

title: Scope-aware session summary (window/source -> summary+rollup+signatures+trend)
description:
Make the session read endpoint SCOPE-AWARE: accept a time window + source and return the scoped summary + rollup + signatures + pass-rate trend buckets, all pre-aggregated. This is what lets every number above the list mean "within this scope" and stay meaningful at any volume.

WHY: At true scale the browser must not hold every raw finding to render the scorecard, compliance counts, sparkline, and signatures. The server computes them over the scoped set.

WHAT (src/api/sessions.ts, GET /api/sessions/:uuid — or a /summary sibling; choose and document):

1. Accept query params:
   - `window`: '15m' | '1h' | '6h' | 'all' (default 'all'). Define the scope as transmissions whose received_at falls in [now - window, now]; 'all' = no time bound.
   - `source`: a source key or 'all' (default 'all').

2. Over the SCOPED transmission set, compute and return:
   - `summary`: computeComplianceSummary over scoped finding counts (existing function — feed it scoped counts).
   - `rollup`: the gradeable passing/failing/untested rollup (currently computed client-side in Dashboard.tsx computeRollup / engine.js rollup) — move/share it server-side so scorecard numbers are scope-relative. Keep the exact spec (gradeable = verified|heuristic; failing folds mixed in).
   - `signatures`: computeSignatures over the scoped set (from the signature-engine issue), pre-aggregated, sorted by count DESC.
   - `trend`: pass-rate buckets via `passTrend(transmissions, 30)` ported from engine.js — 30 buckets across the scope's time span; each bucket `{ tot, fail, rate }` where rate = pass/(pass+fail) or null for empty; a tx "fails" if any finding sev==='fail'. Empty-bucket carry-forward is a RENDER concern (sparkline) — the endpoint returns raw per-bucket {tot,fail,rate}.
   - `sources`: window-aware per-source counts for the filter `<select>` (from the source-dimension issue): [{ source, sourceCode, sourceLabel, count }], computed over the window (NOT further narrowed by the selected source — the dropdown must show all sources' in-window counts).
   - `scoped` totals for the scope readout: total scoped tx, tx-with-failures count, distinct-issue count.

3. Keep existing behavior intact: 404 for unknown/expired uuid, session meta, expiresAt, the per-tx findings drill-down (still needed for the docked detail pane — but see the paginated-list issue for how the list itself is fetched). Decide cleanly whether the full transmission list still ships here or moves entirely to the list endpoint; document the split.

VALIDATION: reject/normalize unknown window/source values gracefully (fall back to defaults rather than 400, to keep the dashboard resilient).

DEPENDS ON: structured findings (for signatures), signature engine, source dimension.
OUT OF SCOPE: the paginated transmission list endpoint (separate issue) and all web rendering.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/sessions/:uuid (or /summary) accepts window(15m|1h|6h|all,default all)+source(key|all,default all); returns scoped summary, server rollup, signatures (sorted), 30-bucket passTrend {tot,fail,rate}, window-aware sources counts, and scope totals {scoped,withFailures,distinctIssues}; unknown values fall back to defaults; 404/meta/expiresAt preserved; list/summary split documented.
close_reason: ac22588 scope-aware GET /api/sessions/:uuid — window+source params, pure src/api/scope.ts (rollup/passTrend/scope helper), scoped summary+rollup+signatures+trend+sources+totals; gates green, clean review

title: Source dimension: code + label + per-source counts
description:
Expose a stable SOURCE dimension on transmissions, with a 3-letter code + full label, and support filtering + per-source counts. Volume comes from "one or multiple CCEs", so every transmission needs a source/device identifier the dashboard can scope by.

WHY: The filter bar's source `<select>` lists "All sources (N)" plus one option per source with its in-window count; each list row shows a 3-letter source code (e.g. KAN) with the full label on hover; signatures report `sourceCount`.

WHAT (backend):

1. The source identifier ALREADY EXISTS as `transmission.transfer_src` (populated from meta.transferSrc by schema.ts; column in 20-transmission.sql; carried by repository TransmissionRow). Use it as the source key — do NOT add a new column. Confirm it is indexed adequately for per-source filtering/counting (add a `(session_uuid, transfer_src)` index in 40-indexes.sql if the scope/count queries need it).

2. Derive a presentation pair from the raw source key:
   - `sourceCode` — a stable 3-letter uppercase code (e.g. "org.kano-depot" → "KAN"). Deterministic from the key (first letters of significant tokens, or first 3 alnum chars uppercased) so the same key always yields the same code; document the rule.
   - `sourceLabel` — a human label (the raw key, or a cleaned version). Full label shown as the row title attr.
   Implement as a small pure helper (e.g. src/api/source.ts) with unit tests, since both the list rows and the filter `<select>` need identical derivation. Handle a null/empty transfer_src → a single "unknown"/"—" bucket with a stable code.

3. Expose `source` (raw key), `sourceCode`, `sourceLabel` on the per-transmission API view (TransmissionView in src/api/sessions.ts + the api.ts mirror — coordinate field names with the api-types issue).

4. Provide per-source counts (window-aware): a helper that, given the scoped transmission set, returns [{ source, sourceCode, sourceLabel, count }] for the filter `<select>` options. This is consumed by the scope-aware summary endpoint.

OUT OF SCOPE: the actual scope/window filtering endpoint (separate issue) and the FilterBar UI. This issue just makes source a first-class, derivable, countable dimension on the backend + types.
acceptance_criteria: transfer_src used as source key (no new column); pure source.ts helper derives stable 3-letter sourceCode + sourceLabel (unit-tested, null bucket handled); source/sourceCode/sourceLabel exposed on the tx view; window-aware per-source counts helper returns [{source,sourceCode,sourceLabel,count}].

title: NEXT BITE: M6 §1.3 auth opt-in (ct4.1-.3)
description:
## Underlying issues

- ct4: [epic] §1.3 auth opt-in (M6) — umbrella
- ct4.1: Credential generation + storage — dashboard generates token+header OR Basic creds; stored HASHED, plaintext shown once
- ct4.2: Stage 2 — enforce auth on ingest: when enabled, require correct credential else 401 (no row)
- ct4.3: Auth opt-in UI + config snippet — dashboard toggle → show generated credential + copy-paste config once

This is DESIGN §14 build-order step 6 (M6). M2 (ingest), M3 (sessions/dashboard API), M4 (web), M5 (semantic checks) are all landed. §1.3 is currently classed ✅(opt-in) in the §7 matrix and reads "Enforced once supplier enables the auth layer" — once this lands and a supplier opts in, the matrix grades 1.3 from real ingest traffic (render-only frontend for the matrix row; NO matrix changes).

## Read first

Memory:
- `bd memories` holds ONLY the M4 frontend-stack decision (React SPA + Vite + @fastify/static, src/web/ talks to the JSON API). Relevant to ct4.3's placement but nothing auth-specific. The §1.3 opt-in framing lives in auto-memory `architecture-decisions.md` and, more usefully, in the DESIGN sections below — reading those suffices.

Documents / code:
- DESIGN.md §3 (auth = "opt-in compliance layer, not a gate"; dashboard generates the credential), §6 stage table row 2 (Auth: "If enabled, expected token header or Basic Auth present & correct → 401"), §10 Setup ("toggle → service generates token + header name or Basic creds → shows config snippet"), §12 ("Auth secrets stored hashed, never echoed after first display"), §14.6.
- src/ingest/route.ts — the **Stage-2 auth INSERTION POINT** comment lives in `preBodyStages()` (after `sessionStage`, before the body stages); a halt here is 401 with NO transmission row (like 404/405). ct4.2 inserts the auth stage there.
- src/ingest/stages/session.ts — stage 0 idiom (injectable `db?`, `getSession`, `halt(404)`). The auth stage mirrors this. NOTE: session stage calls `bumpLastPostAt` on success, BEFORE the auth stage runs — see Recently-decided.
- src/db/repository.ts — `SessionRow` (carries `auth_enabled`, `auth_method`, `auth_header_name`, `auth_secret_hash`), `createSession` (already accepts `authEnabled/authMethod/authHeaderName/authSecretHash` but POST /api/sessions calls it with NO args → auth disabled). NO "enable/disable auth on existing session" helper exists — ct4.1 adds it. NEVER select/return `auth_secret_hash` to clients.
- src/api/sessions.ts — POST /api/sessions (no body, mints auth-disabled), GET /api/sessions/:uuid (already exposes only `auth_enabled`/`auth_method`, never the hash). ct4.1 adds the enable/disable-auth endpoint(s) here.
- src/web/components/Setup.tsx — has an explicit "auth opt-in toggle deferred to M6, NOT rendered here" scope note. ct4.3 removes that note and adds the toggle + credential display + config snippet. src/web/api.ts — the browser client (re-declares types verbatim; ct4.3 adds the new client fn + types here). src/web/routes/Dashboard.tsx — wires Setup's props / refetch.
- db/initdb/10-session.sql — the auth columns already exist (`auth_enabled` default false, `auth_method` CHECK in ('header','basic'), `auth_header_name`, `auth_secret_hash`). NO SQL change needed; verify only.
- src/schema-registry.ts:72 — the only existing hashing in the repo (`createHash('sha256')`). There is NO password-hashing dependency (no bcrypt/scrypt lib) — use node:crypto `scrypt` + `randomBytes` + `timingSafeEqual` (no new dep).

## Recently-decided context

- **No new dependency for hashing.** Use node:crypto `scryptSync`/`scrypt` with a per-secret random salt; store `salt:hash` (hex or base64) in `auth_secret_hash`; verify with `timingSafeEqual`. The §1.3 secret is the bearer token (header method) or the password (basic). sha256 (used for content hashing) is NOT appropriate for a credential — use a salted KDF.
- **Column mapping (internal to the new crypto/credential module — both store and verify go through it, so it is the single source of truth):** header method → `auth_header_name` = the configurable header name (e.g. `X-CCE-Token`), `auth_secret_hash` = KDF(token). basic method → `auth_header_name` = the Basic username, `auth_secret_hash` = KDF(password); verify decodes `Authorization: Basic base64(user:pass)`, checks `user === auth_header_name` AND KDF(pass) matches. This reuses the existing columns with no schema change.
- **Frozen export ct4.2 depends on (this bite's contract — analogous to M5's `SemanticCheck`):** ct4.1 creates `src/auth/credential.ts` exporting BOTH `generateCredential(method, opts)` (returns the plaintext to show once + the `{auth_method, auth_header_name, auth_secret_hash}` to persist) AND `verifyCredential(presented, session)` (returns boolean; `presented` carries the relevant request header value(s); `session` carries the stored auth fields). ct4.2's stage imports `verifyCredential` and does NOT re-implement hashing. ct4.1 OWNS and freezes these signatures before ct4.2/ct4.3 start.
- **Secret shown exactly once (§12):** the enable-auth endpoint returns the plaintext token/password in its response body; it is NEVER returned again. GET /api/sessions/:uuid must keep exposing only `auth_enabled`/`auth_method` (it already does — do not add the hash or plaintext).
- **Auth stage re-fetches the session** (injectable `db?`, like sessionStage) and reads its auth fields, rather than threading the session row through the pipeline — this keeps `src/ingest/pipeline.ts` UNTOUCHED (do NOT widen `PipelineContext`). The extra PK lookup is acceptable for v1 synthetic data. (Threading the row through both stages to avoid the double-fetch is a possible optimization but is OUT OF SCOPE here.)
- **`bumpLastPostAt` ordering wrinkle:** session stage (stage 0) bumps `last_post_at` on success, and runs BEFORE the auth stage (stage 2). So a request that 401s will still have bumped `last_post_at`. KEEP this behavior (do not touch session.ts) — a 401 still proves the session is live for the §11 retention clock; the row simply isn't persisted. Note it; don't fix it.
- **Auth stage no-ops when `auth_enabled = false`** → CONTINUE (zero-friction default; §3). Only when enabled does a missing/incorrect credential halt 401 with no row.
- **§1.3 is INGEST auth only.** Do NOT add auth to the dashboard read API (GET /api/sessions) — the capability URL is the dashboard's bearer authority (§3/§12). The toggle controls only the `/i/{uuid}` ingest path.

## Slicing recommendation

Mirror the M5 pattern: serializing Subagent A owns the shared credential contract + storage + API, then B and C run fully parallel against file-disjoint surfaces.

1. **Subagent A — credential generation + storage (ct4.1)** — runs FIRST; owns the frozen `verifyCredential`/`generateCredential` contract.
   - Reads: DESIGN §3/§6/§10/§12, src/db/repository.ts, src/api/sessions.ts, src/schema-registry.ts (hashing idiom), db/initdb/10-session.sql.
   - Produces: `src/auth/credential.ts` (scrypt-based generate + verify, per the column mapping above; EXPORT + freeze `generateCredential`/`verifyCredential`); a repository helper to enable/disable auth on an existing session (UPDATE `auth_enabled/auth_method/auth_header_name/auth_secret_hash`), NEVER returning the hash to callers; new endpoint(s) on src/api/sessions.ts (e.g. `POST /api/sessions/:uuid/auth` to enable → returns the plaintext credential ONCE + the config it implies; a way to disable). Verify the SQL columns already exist (no change).
   - Acceptance: enabling auth flips the session's auth fields, stores only the salted hash, returns the plaintext exactly once; GET /api/sessions/:uuid still leaks no secret; `verifyCredential` roundtrips (correct → true, wrong/missing → false, timing-safe); build+test+lint green.

2. **Subagent B — stage 2 enforce auth on ingest (ct4.2)** — owns `src/ingest/stages/auth.ts` + the route.ts wiring ONLY.
   - Reads: src/ingest/route.ts (the Stage-2 INSERTION POINT in preBodyStages), src/ingest/stages/session.ts (idiom), src/auth/credential.ts (imports `verifyCredential`), src/ingest/pipeline.ts (FROZEN — do not edit).
   - Produces: `authStage(db?)` that re-fetches the session, CONTINUEs when `auth_enabled=false`, and when enabled calls `verifyCredential` on the request's header(s) → CONTINUE if correct, `halt(401)` (no row) otherwise. Wire it into `preBodyStages()` at the insertion point (after sessionStage). Do NOT touch pipeline.ts, do NOT add a ctx field.
   - Acceptance: auth-disabled session ingests unchanged; enabled + correct token header (or correct Basic) → request proceeds to body stages; enabled + missing/incorrect → 401 with NO transmission row; unit tests for all branches (hand-rolled ctx + injected db / fake session), full-flow DB-gated tests skip gracefully.

3. **Subagent C — auth opt-in UI + config snippet (ct4.3)** — owns `src/web/api.ts`, `src/web/components/Setup.tsx`, and `src/web/routes/Dashboard.tsx` (whatever prop/refetch wiring Setup needs) ONLY. Web-only; depends on A's HTTP contract, NOT A's files.
   - Reads: DESIGN §10, src/web/components/Setup.tsx (remove the "deferred to M6" note), src/web/api.ts (add client fn + response types, re-declared verbatim per the existing convention), src/web/routes/Dashboard.tsx.
   - Produces: an auth opt-in toggle in Setup; on enable, calls the new endpoint and shows the generated credential + a copy-paste config snippet (curl with the token header, or Basic auth) shown ONCE, with a clear "you won't see this again" affordance; reflects `auth_enabled`/`auth_method` from session meta when already on.
   - Acceptance: toggling on calls the API and renders the credential + snippet once; the dashboard shows auth as enabled afterward; `npm run typecheck:web` + lint pass; the matrix/transmissions views are untouched.

Run order: **A first** (owns credential.ts + repository + sessions API; freezes the verify/generate contract), **then B ∥ C fully parallel** — B owns ingest auth stage + route.ts, C owns the three web files; they share NO files. B depends on A's exported `verifyCredential`; C depends on A's HTTP contract only.

## Out of scope

- **src/ingest/pipeline.ts** — FROZEN; do NOT widen `PipelineContext` or change the stage contract. Thread nothing new through ctx (auth stage re-fetches).
- **The M5 semantic stage** and any stage 3-8 code — untouched.
- **Dashboard read-API auth** — the capability URL is the dashboard's authority; do NOT gate GET /api/sessions.
- **Split ingest-vs-view tokens / move-secret-to-header (§12 future production mode)** — NOT v1.
- **Retention worker (M7/yhg)**, polish/fixtures (M8/bat), schema-revision proposals (ven) — separate milestones.
- **Double-fetch optimization** (threading the session row through both stages) — explicitly deferred; re-fetch is fine.
- **DB schema changes** — the auth columns already exist; verify only.

## Commit + test expectations

- Commit to this repo (local-only; no remote → do NOT push). Terse `<prefix>: <summary> (<bd-id>)` style (`git log --oneline` first). Suggested: A `auth: credential generation + storage (ct4.1)`; B `auth: enforce opt-in auth on ingest — stage 2 (ct4.2)`; C `web: auth opt-in toggle + config snippet (ct4.3)`.
- One commit per subagent. Parallel B/C each `git add` ONLY their own files (do NOT `git add -A`; a beads pre-commit hook may re-stage `.beads/issues.jsonl` — expected). If git hits index.lock, wait briefly and retry once.
- Gates green before each commit: `npm run build && npm test && npm run lint` (run `npm run format` to fix style). Build includes `typecheck:web`, so ct4.3's web types are gated there.
- No `bd close` by implementers — the coordinator closes after the clean-context review.
close_reason: ct4.1/.2/.3 all landed and reviewed clean (a9de047/68d0fed/18d937a).

title: NEXT BITE: M5 semantic checks — stage 8 (8ji.1-.4)
description:
## Underlying issues

- 8ji: [epic] Semantic checks (M5) — umbrella
- 8ji.1: Duplicate detection (§1.8) — flag repeated transferId + exact content_hash replays; never silently collapse
- 8ji.2: Interval regularity heuristic (§3.4) — ABST logger-timestamp regularity
- 8ji.3: Concurrency observation (§2.1) — in-memory in-flight request tracking per session
- 8ji.4: Present-object inventory (§3.3 info) — inventory which DS01 objects are present (informational)

This is DESIGN §14 build-order step 5 (M5), the FIRST semantic stage. It plugs into the existing ingest pipeline at the explicit Stage-8 insertion point. M2 (ingest core) and M3/M4 (API + web) are all landed; the §7 matrix already renders rows 1.8/2.1/3.4 (heuristic) and 3.3 (attestation) — once these findings land, the matrix flips AUTOMATICALLY (render-only frontend; NO web changes).

## Read first

Memory:
- The bd memory store (`bd memories`) currently holds ONLY the M4 frontend-stack decision — nothing M5-relevant, so do not chase it. The architecture context (capability-URL model, §1.3 auth opt-in [NOT this bite], the verifiability-spectrum framing the §7 matrix renders) lives in auto-memory `architecture-decisions.md` and, more usefully for a cold agent, in DESIGN §7/§8/§12 cited below — reading those suffices.

Documents / code:
- DESIGN.md §6 (pipeline stage table — stage 8 = semantic checks: 'findings; 2xx (data accepted)'), §7 (matrix classes/render rules for 1.8 🟡, 2.1 🟡, 3.4 🟡, 3.3 📝), §8 (data model + the (session_uuid,content_hash) & (session_uuid,transfer_id) dedup indexes; severity = pass|fail|info), §14.5.
- src/ingest/pipeline.ts — the FROZEN contract. PipelineContext is over-provisioned; stages read/write slots and DO NOT widen the type. Do NOT edit this file. Note `record(ctx, finding)`, `CONTINUE`, `Finding = InsertFindingInput`.
- src/ingest/route.ts — the Stage-8 INSERTION POINT comment lives in `bodyStages()` (after schemaStage, before persist). `persistTransmission` computes content_hash = sha256(ctx.rawBody). The handler builds ctx, runs pre-body then body stages, persists one row + findings.
- src/ingest/stages/*.ts — the one-file-per-stage pattern to mirror (schema.ts shows reading ctx.parsedBody/ctx.meta + emitting findings; size.ts/content-type.ts show pass/fail finding shape).
- src/db/repository.ts — listTransmissions, insertTransmission, insertFindings, FindingRow/Severity. NO 'find prior tx by transferId/hash' helper exists yet — A adds it.

## Recently-decided context

- **Stage 8 is body-side and NEVER halts.** Semantic checks always `record(...)`/return CONTINUE; the data is accepted (2xx). They run AFTER schema (stage 7).
- **Pre-populated context (confirmed):** schema stage (7) sets `ctx.meta.transferId/transferSrc/transferType/schemaVersion`; parse stage (6) sets `ctx.parsedBody`. So stage 8 reads transferId from `ctx.meta.transferId` and the payload from `ctx.parsedBody`. When parseOk!==true / schemaOk!==true, semantic checks should no-op gracefully (nothing to inspect).
- **content_hash for dup detection:** compute `createHash('sha256').update(ctx.rawBody).digest()` IN the duplicate check (route.ts computes its own copy at persist; do not try to share it across the frozen ctx). Query prior transmissions in the SAME session by transfer_id and by content_hash via a NEW repository helper.
- **Severity model drives the matrix:** heuristic rows (1.8/2.1/3.4) only leave 'untested' when a pass OR fail finding exists (deriveStatus in src/api/compliance-matrix.ts ignores `info`). So gradeable checks emit **pass when clean, fail when the heuristic trips** (per-transmission), with the 'can't judge justification' caveat in the finding `detail`. Inventory (3.3) is classed 📝 attestation → its status is ALWAYS 'self-attestation' regardless of counts, so 8ji.4 emits `info` findings that surface in drill-down only (never flips the row) — this is correct/honest, not a bug.
- **Concurrency (§2.1) is cross-cutting in-memory state**, NOT a pure per-request stage: it needs an in-flight counter incremented at handler entry and decremented in a finally, with the concurrent-count snapshot taken at entry. This touches route.ts (a shared file) → it lands with the serializing agent A, not a parallel stage.
- **§8 dedup indexes** ((session_uuid,content_hash), (session_uuid,transfer_id)) must exist in the first-boot SQL — A verifies/adds them.

## Slicing recommendation

Mirror the M4 pattern: a serializing Subagent A owns the shared files (route.ts wiring, repository.ts helper, the concurrency tracker + route.ts plumbing, the semantic.ts orchestrator + stub check files with a FROZEN check-function signature) AND lands the cross-cutting concurrency check. Then B/C/D fill one file-disjoint check each.

1. **Subagent A — scaffold + concurrency (8ji.3)** — runs FIRST; serializes route.ts, repository.ts, the DB init SQL, and creates the shared stage + stubs.
   - Reads: pipeline.ts (frozen contract), route.ts (insertion point + persist), schema.ts (finding idiom), repository.ts, DESIGN §6/§7/§8.
   - Produces:
     - `src/ingest/stages/semantic.ts` — a single `semanticStage(deps)` wired into route.ts `bodyStages()` at the Stage-8 insertion point (after schemaStage). It composes four check functions and pushes their findings. Define + EXPORT a FROZEN check signature for B/C/D, e.g. `export type SemanticCheck = (ctx: PipelineContext, deps: SemanticDeps) => Finding[] | Promise<Finding[]>`, and create FOUR stub files A's orchestrator imports: `stages/semantic/duplicate.ts`, `interval.ts`, `concurrency.ts`, `inventory.ts` (concurrency A implements; the other three are stubs returning []).
     - Concurrency tracker: `src/ingest/concurrency-tracker.ts` (in-memory Map<sessionUuid, inflightCount>), with route.ts handler incrementing on entry and decrementing in a finally; capture the concurrent-count snapshot at entry and thread it to semanticStage as a dep (do NOT add a ctx field — ctx is frozen). Implement `concurrency.ts`: pass when the session was serial (snapshot ≤1), fail when ≥1 other request was in flight (§2.1 'serial delivery by default').
     - repository helper(s): e.g. `findPriorTransmissions(sessionUuid, {transferId, contentHash})` for the duplicate check; add the §8 indexes to the first-boot SQL if absent.
   - Acceptance: semanticStage runs after schema and never halts (2xx preserved); concurrency findings emitted under requirement 2.1 (pass/fail) with the tracker decremented even on throw; build+test+lint green; the three stub checks return [] so the pipeline is green before B/C/D land.

2. **Subagent B — duplicate detection (8ji.1)** — owns `src/ingest/stages/semantic/duplicate.ts` only.
   - Uses A's repository helper + `createHash('sha256').update(ctx.rawBody)` + `ctx.meta.transferId`. Emit requirement 1.8: **pass** when transferId+hash are novel in the session, **fail** when a repeat is observed (detail names which: same transferId vs exact content replay; note justification can't be judged). Never collapse.
   - Acceptance: a second POST with a repeated transferId (or identical body) yields a 1.8 fail finding on the new transmission; a novel one yields a 1.8 pass.

3. **Subagent C — interval regularity (8ji.2)** — owns `src/ingest/stages/semantic/interval.ts` only.
   - Reads ctx.parsedBody ABST objects' logger timestamps; heuristic regularity over intervals. Emit requirement 3.4: pass when regular, fail (or the heuristic's honest verdict) when irregular; no-op when <2 timestamps or unparsed.
   - Acceptance: a regular series → 3.4 pass; an irregular series → 3.4 fail; sparse/empty → no finding.

4. **Subagent D — present-object inventory (8ji.4)** — owns `src/ingest/stages/semantic/inventory.ts` only.
   - Reads ctx.parsedBody; emit requirement 3.3 **info** finding listing which DS01 object types are present (count per type). Informational only — does NOT grade (matrix keeps 3.3 'self-attestation').
   - Acceptance: a payload with N object types → one 3.3 info finding inventorying them; surfaces in transmission drill-down.

Run order: **A first** (owns route.ts, repository.ts, semantic.ts, tracker, stubs, init SQL), **then B ∥ C ∥ D fully parallel** (each owns exactly one file under stages/semantic/, file-disjoint; none touches route.ts/repository.ts/semantic.ts/each other). Each implementer adds unit tests in the node:test harness (pure check logic testable without a DB; duplicate's repository helper test may be DB-gated/skipped like existing DB tests; the concurrency tracker is in-memory → fully testable).

## Out of scope

- **Active-harness checks (§4 retry/backoff/Retry-After/abandon)** — deferred to a future milestone (DESIGN §15). NOT M5.
- **§5 guided retransmission** — deferred.
- **§1.3 auth opt-in (M6/ct4)** — there is a separate auth INSERTION POINT in route.ts preBodyStages; do NOT wire auth in this bite.
- **Frontend** — the §7 matrix + transmissions drill-down already render whatever findings land (render-only). Do NOT touch src/web.
- **pipeline.ts** — frozen; do NOT edit the context/stage contract. Do NOT change the persistence boundary.

## Commit + test expectations

- Commit to this repo (local-only; do NOT push — no remote). Terse `<prefix>: <summary> (<bd-ids>)` style; suggested prefix `ingest:` (matches recent semantic/pipeline commits).
- One commit per subagent: A `ingest: stage 8 scaffold + concurrency observation (8ji.3)`; B `ingest: duplicate detection (8ji.1)`; C `ingest: interval regularity heuristic (8ji.2)`; D `ingest: present-object inventory (8ji.4)`.
- Parallel B/C/D each `git add` ONLY their one check file + its test (do NOT `git add -A`); a beads pre-commit hook may re-stage .beads/issues.jsonl (expected). If git hits index.lock, wait briefly and retry once.
- Gates green before each commit: `npm run build && npm test && npm run lint` (run `npm run format` to fix style). Note build now includes typecheck:web (M5 touches no web, so it just passes).
- No `bd close` by implementers — the coordinator closes after the clean-context review.

title: NEXT BITE: M3 sessions & dashboard read API (43b.1-.3)
description:
## Underlying issues

- cce-data-delivery-validator-43b: [epic] Sessions & dashboard read API (M3) — umbrella
- 43b.1: POST /api/sessions — mint v4 UUID, create session row, return {uuid, ingestUrl, dashboardUrl}
- 43b.2: GET /api/sessions/{uuid} — reverse-chron transmissions, per-tx findings, drill-down (raw body, status, parsed body)
- 43b.3: Compliance summary computation — aggregate findings into the §7 verifiability matrix with live counts + honesty classification

This is the **read side** that exposes what M2 (ingest) persists. It is the DESIGN §14 build-order step 3 and unblocks M4 (web UI yih.*), M6 (auth ct4.1), and gives the dashboard its data.

## Read first

`bd memories` is still empty — knowledge lives in code + DESIGN.md. Read:

- `DESIGN.md` §5 (onboarding: the exact POST /api/sessions response shape — `{uuid, ingestUrl:"/i/{uuid}", dashboardUrl:"/d/{uuid}"}`), §7 (THE verifiability matrix — the 27-row class table the summary encodes), §8 (transmission/finding columns + the `(session_uuid, received_at DESC)` index the list query uses), §10 (dashboard sections: what the GET must surface — setup, compliance summary, reverse-chron transmissions w/ drill-down, lifecycle clock).
- `~/.claude/projects/-home-benson-sandbox-phoenixgh-cce-data-delivery-validator/memory/architecture-decisions.md` — locked decisions (capability-URL onboarding, §1.3 auth opt-in default-OFF, the verifiability-spectrum framing that drives the §7 summary). A spawned subagent may not inherit this auto-memory; read it explicitly.
- The M1/M2 surfaces you build ON (read before writing):
  - `src/app.ts` — `buildApp()` is the factory; routes are registered here (see `registerIngestRoute(app)` call). Register the new API the same way.
  - `src/ingest/route.ts` — the route-module pattern to mirror: a `registerIngestRoute(app)` exporting a `app.route({...})`/handler, driven in tests by `app.inject`. Also shows the `reply.code(n).send(obj)` JSON-response idiom.
  - `src/db/repository.ts` — existing `createSession`, `getSession`, `insertTransmission`, `insertFinding(s)`, plus types `SessionRow`, `TransmissionRow`, `FindingRow`, `Severity`, `Queryable`. All take an optional `db: Queryable`. M3 ADDS read functions here.
  - `src/db/index.ts` — the barrel that re-exports repo symbols; add new exports here too.

## Recently-decided context

M2 (ingest pipeline core) landed this session across commits **6854b3f, a47509f, 4dcf0ba, adf3d76, 29c09a7**. Integration facts the executing agent MUST know — NOT in the issue descriptions:

- **The request body is NOT auto-parsed for ANY route.** `src/app.ts` calls `removeAllContentTypeParsers()` + a catch-all `parseAs:'buffer'`, so `request.body` is a raw `Buffer` on every route (this is for §1.4 wire-byte fidelity on ingest). **POST /api/sessions takes NO request body** (it mints with auth-disabled defaults — auth config is M6), so this is a non-issue for 43b.1 *as long as the handler does not try to read/parse a JSON body*. Do NOT add a JSON body parser (it would break ingest's raw-body contract). If you ever need request JSON on an API route, parse `request.body` (the Buffer) yourself — but M3 should not need to.
- **JSON RESPONSES still work normally.** `removeAllContentTypeParsers` affects REQUEST parsing only; `reply.send(object)` serializes to JSON as usual (the ingest route already returns JSON objects and tests read `res.json()`). So returning `{...}` from handlers is fine.
- **`ingestUrl`/`dashboardUrl` are RELATIVE paths** (`/i/{uuid}`, `/d/{uuid}`), exactly per §5 — not absolute URLs. The frontend composes the origin. `/d/{uuid}` (the web UI) does NOT exist yet (M4); the API just returns the path string — that's correct.
- **Sessions are minted with auth DISABLED.** `createSession()` already defaults `auth_enabled=false`. 43b.1 calls it with no auth input. The session table has auth columns but M3 leaves them at defaults (M6/ct4.1 sets them).
- **Findings exist only for the requirements M2 grades so far** — the pipeline emits findings for **1.1** (parse), **1.2** (content-type), **1.4** (size), **1.6** (encoding), **3.1/3.2** (schema). Semantic-check findings (**1.8, 2.1, 3.3, 3.4**) are M5 and are NOT emitted yet. The compliance summary MUST handle requirements with **zero findings gracefully** (render them as "no data yet / untested", not crash or show a false pass).
- **404 contract:** `GET /api/sessions/{unknown-uuid}` → **404**. `POST /api/sessions` always succeeds (mint) — recommend **201 Created**. Unknown-method handling on these paths can rely on Fastify defaults (no need for the all-methods 405 trick the ingest route uses — that was a §1.1 requirement specific to ingest).
- **Lifecycle/expiry** (§10) is derivable, not stored: `expiresAt = (last_post_at ?? created_at) + 30 days`. The GET response MAY include an `expiresAt` computed field (nice for M4's lifecycle section), but keep it minimal — the worker that ACTS on it is M7 (out of scope).

## Slicing recommendation

New code lives under a new `src/api/` dir. The mint endpoint and the GET endpoint share the route module (`src/api/sessions.ts`), so they serialize; the §7 matrix is a pure, file-disjoint module that parallelizes.

1. **Subagent A — 43b.1 POST /api/sessions** (establishes the api module; runs first).
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §5; `src/app.ts`, `src/ingest/route.ts` (route-module pattern), `src/db/repository.ts` (`createSession`).
   - Produces: `src/api/sessions.ts` exporting `registerSessionsApi(app)`; a `POST /api/sessions` handler that calls `createSession()` and returns **201** `{ uuid, ingestUrl: ` + "`/i/${uuid}`" + `, dashboardUrl: ` + "`/d/${uuid}`" + ` }`. Wire `registerSessionsApi(app)` into `buildApp()` next to `registerIngestRoute(app)`.
   - Acceptance: `app.inject` POST /api/sessions → 201 + the three-field body; a row exists in `session`. DB-touching tests skip-guarded per `src/db/repository.test.ts`.

2. **Subagent C — 43b.3 compliance summary** (PURE module; file-disjoint; parallel with A).
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §7 (the full matrix + the render rules at the end: ✅/🟡 carry live pass/fail counts; 🔌 "not yet exercised"; 📝 "self-attestation"; 🔒 "enforced"); the architecture-decisions memory (verifiability spectrum).
   - Produces: `src/api/compliance-matrix.ts` — the §7 matrix encoded as STATIC data (all 27 rows: `requirement`, `summary`, `class` — handle the split classes 1.1=✅/🔒 and 4.4=🔌/📝, and 1.7="—" nothing-to-grade), plus a PURE `computeComplianceSummary(findingCounts)` that joins live counts (per requirement → {pass, fail, info}) onto the static matrix and derives each row's display status (e.g. `pass`/`fail`/`mixed`/`untested` for ✅/🟡; `not-exercised` for 🔌; `self-attestation` for 📝; `enforced` for 🔒). Zero findings for a gradeable row → `untested`.
   - Acceptance: unit tests (no DB) over `computeComplianceSummary`: a row with live pass-only → pass; with a fail → fail/mixed; a 🔌 row → not-exercised regardless of counts; a 📝 row → self-attestation; an ungraded ✅ row with no findings → untested. All 27 requirements present in the output.

3. **Subagent B — 43b.2 GET /api/sessions/{uuid}** (after A — shares `sessions.ts`; consumes C's pure fn).
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §8, §10; A's `src/api/sessions.ts`; C's `src/api/compliance-matrix.ts`; `src/db/repository.ts`.
   - Produces: new read repo fns in `repository.ts` (thin, no business logic): `listTransmissions(sessionUuid)` (reverse-chron via the `(session_uuid, received_at DESC)` index) and a findings reader (`listFindingsForSession(sessionUuid)` joined, or `listFindingsByTransmission`). Export them from `db/index.ts`. Add `GET /api/sessions/:uuid` to `sessions.ts`: 404 if `getSession` returns null; else return `{ session: <metadata>, transmissions: [ { ...drill-down: http_status, content_type, content_encoding, wire_bytes, parse_ok, schema_ok, body, raw_body, findings:[{requirement,severity,detail,pointer}] } ], summary: computeComplianceSummary(<counts>) }`. Optionally include `expiresAt`.
   - Acceptance: GET unknown uuid → 404; GET a session minted via `createSession()` with a couple of `insertTransmission`+`insertFinding` rows → 200 with reverse-chron transmissions, each carrying its findings + drill-down fields, and a `summary` block reflecting the seeded findings. DB-skip-guarded; run live once.

Run order: **A ∥ C, then B.** B shares `sessions.ts` with A (so after A) and imports C's pure module (so after C). A and C are file-disjoint → parallel. Commits serialize regardless (the implement-next coordinator handles that).

## Out of scope

- **Web UI (M4, yih.*)** — M3 is JSON API only. No HTML, no `/d/{uuid}` route; that path is just a string in the POST response.
- **Auth on session creation / enforcement (M6, ct4.*)** — 43b.1 mints with auth disabled. Do not add credential generation or the `X-...`/Basic enforcement; leave the session auth columns at defaults.
- **Semantic-check findings (M5, 8ji.*)** — the summary must tolerate their absence (untested rows), but do NOT compute 1.8/2.1/3.3/3.4 here.
- **Retention worker (M7, yhg.1)** — deriving/returning `expiresAt` is fine; the periodic DELETE sweep is not in scope.
- Do not add a JSON request-body parser or otherwise touch the M1 raw-body/trustProxy wiring in `app.ts` (consume it).

## Commit + test expectations

- Commit to this repo (local-only; **do not push** — no remote). Match the terse `<prefix>: <summary> (<bd-ids>)` style from `git log --oneline` (e.g. `ingest: …`, `db: …`). Suggested prefix: `api:`.
- One commit per subagent boundary (e.g. A: `api: POST /api/sessions mint endpoint (43b.1)`; C: `api: §7 compliance summary computation (43b.3)`; B: `api: GET /api/sessions read + drill-down (43b.2)`).
- Gates green before each commit: `npm run build && npm test && npm run lint` (run `npm run format` to fix style). DB-dependent tests use the skip-guard from `src/db/repository.test.ts` so `npm test` stays green without Postgres; the read/persist paths must ALSO be run live at least once against `docker compose up -d postgres` (`DATABASE_URL=postgresql://cce_validator:cce_validator@localhost:5432/cce_validator npm test`) — paste the round-trip output in the agent report.

title: size: Fastify default bodyLimit (1MB) pre-empts the §1.4 size stage 413
description:
DESIGN.md §6 (lines ~89-90) says 'the app owns the §1.4 cap' so an oversized POST yields our teaching 413 + a recorded transmission row + a 1.4 finding. But app.ts builds Fastify WITHOUT setting bodyLimit, so Fastify's DEFAULT 1MB limit (== our cap) rejects any over-cap body FIRST with FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE: status 413 but body shape {statusCode,code,error,message} (not our {status,findings,transmissionId}) and NO transmission row / NO 1.4 finding persisted. Net: the §1.4 size stage's 413 path is unreachable end-to-end and the teaching finding is never recorded. Fix lives in app.ts (NOT a body stage): raise Fastify bodyLimit above 1MB (e.g. 1MB + headroom, or 2MB) so over-cap bodies REACH the size stage, which then emits the 1.4 finding and halts 413 with a persisted row. The size stage logic itself is correct (verified by a direct unit test at exactly 1_048_577 bytes). Discovered while landing the size stage (3bn.4).

## Context
Subagent B, M2 ingest body stages
close_reason: app.ts raises Fastify bodyLimit to 2 MiB (DEFAULT_BODY_LIMIT) above the §1.4 1MB grading cap, so oversized-but-bounded bodies reach the size stage → our 413 + 1.4 finding + persisted row; full-flow test added

title: persist: raw_body text column rejects NUL bytes from gzip/binary wire bodies (500)
description:
When a request arrives Content-Encoding: gzip (or any binary body), route.ts persistTransmission stores rawBody: ctx.rawBody.toString('utf8'). The compressed wire bytes contain 0x00 (NUL), which Postgres text columns reject: 'invalid byte sequence for encoding UTF8: 0x00'. The whole insert throws -> the ingest handler returns 500 instead of the stage's intended status (200 for a valid gzip happy path, 400 for an undecodable/double-encoded gzip). Repro: POST gzipSync(JSON) to /i/:uuid with content-encoding: gzip -> 500. Discovered while landing the encoding stage (3bn.4). Fix lives in the persist/repo layer (NOT a body stage): e.g. store raw_body as bytea, or store the size-bounded DECODED text when an encoding was applied, or strip/escape NULs. Coordinate with whoever owns route.ts/repository. The encoding+parse stages themselves are correct (verified by direct unit tests).

## Context
Subagent B, M2 ingest body stages
close_reason: route.ts storedRawBody() persists decoded (gzip) text, NUL-stripped, so the raw_body text column never rejects binary bodies; gzip happy path now 200 not 500; full-flow test added

title: No test covers the sessions.ts outdated tally that makes 2kx's fix reachable
description:
2kx (dd999b8) fixed deriveStatus() and unit-tested it well in src/api/compliance-matrix.test.ts (7 cases: outdated-only, current-only, mixed, fail-dominates, none, non-gradeable, omitted-map). But the ONLY path that turns a real session's findings into that input is one line of plumbing in src/api/sessions.ts:407:

    if (f.outdated) scopedOutdated[f.requirement] = (scopedOutdated[f.requirement] ?? 0) + 1;

and nothing exercises it. The endpoint-level summary test — src/api/sessions.test.ts:93 'GET /api/sessions/:uuid -> 200 with reverse-chron transmissions, findings, and §7 summary' — seeds only findings with outdated:false (lines 182, 195) and asserts byReq.get('3.2') === 'untested' (line 208). No test anywhere asserts that a session whose §3.2 findings are severity=info + outdated=true reports status 'pass-outdated'.

That is exactly the user-visible claim in 2kx's acceptance criteria: 'A session using only an older-but-valid schema version no longer displays as untested.' Today a regression that dropped or mistyped the tally line (e.g. tallying into scopedCounts, or reading a field the FindingView projection stopped emitting) would leave every unit test green while restoring the 'untested' lie on the wire.

Ask: add one DB-gated case to src/api/sessions.test.ts — seed a transmission with a §3.2 info finding carrying outdated=true, GET /api/sessions/:uuid, assert summary row 3.2 status === 'pass-outdated' and outdated === 1, and that rollup.passing counts it (scope.ts:136). No behaviour change; the code under test is believed correct.

Also worth folding in: scopedOutdated at src/api/sessions.ts:406 is declared as a bare Record<string, number> even though compliance-matrix.ts exports OutdatedCountsByRequirement for exactly this (scopedCounts on the line above does use its named type).

title: 9mu's COMMENT ON COLUMN fix cannot reach an existing database: edited 10-session.sql in place, no numbered DDL
description:
f167fb8 (9mu) corrected 'Drives 30-day retention' to '7-day' by editing db/initdb/10-session.sql:42 in place, and says so in the commit message ('Databases initialized before this commit keep the stale column comment until they are re-initialized').

This declines both the house rule and 9mu's explicit instruction:
  - CLAUDE.md:132 - 'DDL is ordered and commented - new schema goes in a new numbered file.'
  - 9mu's own text - 'Fix is comment-only (plus one COMMENT ON COLUMN, which needs a new numbered DDL file per the house rule, not an edit to 10-session.sql).'

The deviation is not cosmetic. db/initdb/*.sql runs only when the Postgres data directory is empty, so an in-place edit reaches nothing that already exists. 9mu's stated harm was '\d+ session in any deployment reports the wrong window' - and that harm is untouched on every developer machine with an existing pgdata volume. 9mu records that such machines exist: 50-session-auth-bearer.sql 'must be applied and ... developer machines missed it' (the finding that motivated the 7f53692 CI DDL loop). A 60-*.sql carrying just the corrected COMMENT ON COLUMN is an artifact those machines can apply; an edited 10-session.sql is not.

Secondary cost: db/initdb no longer matches any database initialized before f167fb8, with no migration file to explain the divergence - the exact state the numbering convention exists to prevent. ColdchainDB treats this directory as the house DB-schema style (CLAUDE.md), so the precedent travels.

The rest of 9mu landed correctly: the 10-session.sql:5 header comment, repository.ts:479, CLAUDE.md:118 and docker-compose.yml:18-19 (e2a8b87) are all right, and fresh inits now report 7 days.

Follow-up, not an acceptance break - P3, comment-only impact.

The two doc passages that asserted the absence of that signal - and that c64's own description quoted as its justification - were not updated, so the docs now understate the tooling.

Verifying the contract / What it cannot check': 'X-Forwarded-Proto has no assertable surface today: 1.1 is classified enforced by us in the 7 matrix and the app emits no scheme finding, so term 1 is verified by config review plus TRUSTED_PROXY agreement - not by the script.' The clause about deploy/smoke-proxy-contract.sh remains true (the script still cannot check it), but 'no assertable surface today' is now false: the log line is the surface, and a bring-up check can grep for it.

title: 3b3's 'refused unread' clause is false for tx.undecodable_body and tx.double_encoded
description:
6e51908 (3b3) replaced one unconditional mechanism claim with four evidence-gated tails in describeStoredCopy (src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx:663-696). The 'intact' tail reintroduces a smaller version of the same defect.

src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx:684-687:

    'Every wire byte is present and none reads as undecodable, so the body appears
     to have been MISLABELLED rather than actually ${encoding}-encoded. It was
     refused unread either way, so nothing below is graded payload.'

'Refused unread' is true only for tx.unsupported_encoding, where src/ingest/stages/encoding.ts:61-71 rejects a non-gzip token before touching a byte. The branch is entered for all three codes in ENCODING_REJECTED_CODES (TransmissionsCard.tsx:572-576), and the other two DO read the body:
  - tx.undecodable_body - encoding.ts:73-85 calls gunzipSync(ctx.rawBody) and reports the failure reason;
  - tx.double_encoded - encoding.ts:88-96 decompresses successfully and then inspects the OUTPUT for gzip magic.

The realistic hit is base64-of-gzip, which encoding.ts:76 names explicitly: Content-Encoding: gzip on ASCII base64 text yields stored == wire, replacementDense false -> intact = true -> the note tells the supplier the body was 'refused unread' when it was in fact read and gunzip-attempted.

Same species as 3b3: an unconditional mechanism claim the row does not support. The evidence to gate it is already in hand - decodeState() has just matched the finding code, so the tail can branch on unsupported_encoding vs the read-and-failed codes.

Low severity: the operative sentence ('nothing below is graded payload') is true on every path, and the 'MISLABELLED' framing is defensible for base64-of-gzip. It is the mechanism half that overreaches.

Note also there is no web test harness in this repo (no *.test.tsx under src/web), so none of the four new tails has coverage; that is a convention gap, not this commit's fault.

title: CI workflow has no permissions block and double-runs on PRs
description:
Follow-up on 7f53692 (.github/workflows/ci.yml). Two hardening/hygiene gaps, neither breaking dkz.14 acceptance:

1. NO least-privilege token. The workflow declares no top-level `permissions:`, so every job gets the repository/org DEFAULT GITHUB_TOKEN scope — commonly contents:write on repos created before the read-only default. This job only needs to read the checkout. For a repo explicitly on the publish-readiness track (dkz epic), a public workflow running third-party actions with a write-scoped token is the standard supply-chain finding. Add at the top of ci.yml:

     permissions:
       contents: read

2. DUPLICATE RUNS. `on:` declares both `push: branches: ['**']` and `pull_request` (ci.yml:17-20). A same-repo PR branch therefore triggers two identical runs per push — one from push, one from pull_request. Either scope push to the default branch, or add a concurrency group that cancels superseded runs:

     concurrency:
       group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
       cancel-in-progress: true

Verified during review: the workflow is otherwise sound. Desk-check plus local rehearsal confirmed the DDL loop applies 10..50 cleanly to a fresh database and the suite then runs 272/272 with 0 skips against it, so the no-skip guard enforces real coverage rather than failing spuriously.
close_reason: 24694af ci.yml permissions contents:read + push scoped to main + concurrency group
