title: RETENTION_SWEEP_MS is unreachable under compose and .env.example implies otherwise
description:
Found during lys/dkz.13 review (fc2dcd0).

.env.example:74-75 heads the APP-LEVEL block with: 'Under compose these are supplied by docker-compose.yml and the values here are inert. Export them yourself when running the app directly.' That is true for PORT, HOST, DATABASE_URL and PG* (docker-compose.yml sets all of them literally on the app service), but FALSE for RETENTION_SWEEP_MS (.env.example:99-102): docker-compose.yml never mentions it, and since compose reads .env only for ${...} interpolation (no env_file:, no dotenv dependency — both verified), a value set in .env never reaches the container.

Failure scenario: an operator on the documented production path (compose + edge profile) sets RETENTION_SWEEP_MS=300000 in .env, restarts, and the sweep still runs hourly. .env.example sends them to docker-compose.yml to find the value compose supposedly supplies — where it does not exist. Net effect: the retention sweep cadence is not tunable at all under compose, and no doc says so.

Fix options: (a) add 'RETENTION_SWEEP_MS: ${RETENTION_SWEEP_MS:-3600000}' to the app service environment so the .env value is actually honoured (matches how TRUSTED_PROXY is wired), then the block preamble becomes true; or (b) keep it app-only and say plainly in the RETENTION_SWEEP_MS comment that compose does not pass it through, so under compose the 1 h default is fixed.

docs/deployment.md §4's table is accurate as written (it only claims src/index.ts reads it); only .env.example's block preamble overclaims.
close_reason: 38e3645 option (a): RETENTION_SWEEP_MS wired through compose; .env.example truthful

title: Serve schema {version, sha256} from the API so dashboard provenance cannot drift
description: Found during lys/dkz.7 (a12078a): Setup.tsx carried a fabricated hash ('9f2a…c1' — hash of nothing) precisely because the provenance line is a hardcoded string. The registry already computes the true sha256 at boot (RegistryEntry.sha256) but no API surfaces it; registerSessionsApi has no registry handle. Fix: expose {version, sha256} (e.g. on the session response or a small /api/meta endpoint), render it in Setup.tsx instead of the literal, and drop the hardcoded string. Needs API plumbing + tests, which is why the lys bite corrected the literal but did not do this.

title: Supplier-facing §3.1 guidance still narrows the fail set to z-prefixed keys (tdx's carried-over 'consider' item)
description:
tdx corrected DESIGN.md §7 row 3.1 + §6 (commit 7a9ad12) to say the §3.1 fail set is scan.custom PLUS scan.misnamed (custom by elimination). tdx's own text asked to 'Consider whether requirementReference 3.1 guidance should be widened in the same pass'; its acceptance criteria covered DESIGN only, so with tdx closed the narrowing is now unowned in the two places that remain — including the only SUPPLIER-FACING one.

- src/web/components/requirementReference.ts:100 (§3.1 guidance, shipped in the dashboard's requirement drawer): 'manufacturer-specific data objects (lower-case and "z"-prefixed, e.g. ztpcm) must be described by a schema carried in meta.customDataSchema. Send custom objects without it and this fails'. A supplier whose payload carries customTemp or zTPCM gets a §3.1 FAIL that this guidance says should not apply to them — src/ingest/stages/semantic/custom-schema.ts:209 grades [...scan.custom, ...scan.misnamed], and classify() (lines 143-152) puts every non-z-prefixed, non-DS01-shaped, non-mis-cased key in misnamed.
- src/api/compliance-matrix.ts:130 — the §3.1 row comment carries the same 'custom (clause 4.5 z-prefixed) data objects' framing.

Low severity: the emitted finding detail is itself accurate (it names the offending keys and says they 'read as manufacturer-specific but are not lower-case and z-prefixed'), and the companion naming info finding explains the deviation, so a supplier who opens the finding is not misled — only one who reads the requirement drawer first. But DESIGN and the shipped guidance now disagree, which is the drift 3yu/tdx exist to prevent.

Suggested wording, mirroring the corrected DESIGN cell: '...manufacturer-specific data objects — lower-case "z"-prefixed names as clause 4.5 requires, plus any object name that is neither a DS01 code nor a mis-cased one and therefore reads as custom (e.g. customTemp, zTPCM) — must be described by a schema carried in meta.customDataSchema.'
close_reason: d4699ff §3.1 guidance widened to z-prefixed plus custom-by-elimination

title: (BUG) Rejected-encoding note asserts substitution and unreadability that a mislabeled plain body did not undergo
description:
src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx:658-666 (describeStoredCopy, the new 'rejected' branch from 9f08a60, bug vul).

The branch is entered whenever the row carries tx.unsupported_encoding / tx.undecodable_body / tx.double_encoded, and it renders a FIXED sentence:

  'Not decoded: the ${encoding} encoding was rejected before the body was decompressed, so this copy is the ${encoding} bytes as sent, read as text — X bytes stored from Y bytes on the wire, undecodable bytes substituted and NUL bytes stripped. This is NOT readable payload.'

Two of those clauses are asserted without evidence, and are false in the most likely producing case: a supplier that MISLABELS a plain body. src/ingest/stages/encoding.ts:63-71 rejects any non-gzip token BEFORE looking at a single body byte, so 'Content-Encoding: br' (or deflate, or base64) on an ordinary UTF-8 JSON body halts 400 with tx.unsupported_encoding, and src/ingest/route.ts storedRawBody() then stores the wire bytes verbatim — valid UTF-8, no U+FFFD, no NUL to strip.

The inspector then renders that perfectly readable JSON (RawPayload falls back to raw_body whenever body is null, TransmissionsCard.tsx:723-726) directly beside a note claiming 'undecodable bytes substituted' and 'This is NOT readable payload' — with 'X bytes stored from Y bytes on the wire' showing X == Y on the same line, contradicting the substitution claim it just made.

This is the same species of defect vul filed (an unconditional claim about the stored copy that the row does not support), reintroduced on the other side of the split. vul's fix direction anticipated it: 'otherwise fall through to the wire-size comparison so the >wire case reports substitution honestly' — the landed branch hardcodes the comparison's conclusion instead of computing it.

Not P2: the branch's headline claim ('Not decoded', warn tone) is TRUE on every path that reaches it, so vul's acceptance (derive decodedness from evidence rather than the Content-Encoding header) is met; only the trailing mechanism/readability clauses overreach.

Suggested fix: in the rejected branch, state the substitution/NUL clauses conditionally — the same evidence the function already has (stored vs wire, or replacementDense()) distinguishes 'the copy is binary read as text' from 'the copy is readable text that was merely labelled with an encoding we refuse'.
close_reason: 6e51908 rejected-encoding note now evidence-conditional (follow-up xiz filed for the intact tail)

title: Dev mode serves raw src/web/index.html; add dev:web Vite script or guard static registration
description: Found during dkz.2 README work (62eb9ae): in dev, buildApp() resolves DEFAULT_WEB_DIST to src/web, which holds the untransformed Vite index.html (<script src="/main.tsx">), so the SPA fallback serves a page whose module request 404s. There is no dev:web script. The README consequently says npm run dev hot-reloads the API only and that npm run build (or docker compose up -d) puts the UI on :3000. Fix options: (a) add a dev:web Vite dev-server script with an /api (+ /i, /d, /api/sessions) proxy; (b) guard the static registration so dev mode never serves raw src/web. Either way, update README's dev section when done.

title: Make the TRUSTED_PROXY misconfiguration fail loud: log once when X-Forwarded-Proto arrives from an untrusted address
description:
Follow-up to dkz.4 (commit 421ea96). Not a defect in that commit — the failure mode is documented as the criteria required.

dkz.4's own thesis is 'a self-hoster who misses any of these gets no error'. Two of the three contract terms now have a loud check: term 2 and term 3 are caught by deploy/smoke-proxy-contract.sh (verified: it goes red against a Caddy with max_size 512KB, green against the shipped config). Term 1 has none — docs/deployment.md §6 says so explicitly: 'X-Forwarded-Proto has no assertable surface today ... term 1 is verified by config review plus TRUSTED_PROXY agreement, not by the script.'

And the shipped default lands in exactly the broken state: docker-compose.yml:47 sets TRUSTED_PROXY=${TRUSTED_PROXY:-127.0.0.1}, but under the `edge` profile the proxy is a container on the bridge network, so the out-of-the-box `docker compose --profile edge up -d` silently ignores X-Forwarded-Proto until the operator sets .env. Both the compose comment and deployment.md §2 term 1 say so — but only to a reader who reads them.

Cheap detection exists: the app can compare at request time. If the request carries an X-Forwarded-Proto header but request.protocol still reads 'http' (i.e. Fastify's proxyFn rejected the socket address), the trust scope and the actual proxy disagree. Log it once per process at warn level naming TRUSTED_PROXY, and/or surface it on the dashboard next to the §1.1 'enforced by us' claim.

Scope note: keep it observational. Do not start rejecting or emitting a §1.1 finding — DESIGN.md §7 row 1.1 classifies HTTPS as 🔒 enforced by us, and src/ingest/stages/method.ts is deliberately lenient on scheme.
close_reason: 6c0210a warn-once on untrusted X-Forwarded-Proto, observational only, +2 tests

title: docs/deployment.md §3 tells operators not to guess the compose subnet, then the example guesses 172.16.0.0/12
description:
docs/deployment.md:138-153 (added in 421ea96, dkz.4).

The section reads, in order:
  1. "Find the compose network's subnet before setting it, rather than guessing:" followed by a `docker network inspect` one-liner that yields the real subnet (here: 172.x.0.0/16).
  2. A dotenv block that is the thing an operator copy-pastes: `TRUSTED_PROXY=172.16.0.0/12` — i.e. the guess the previous sentence told them not to make.
  3. "Scope it as tightly as the topology allows: every address you trust is an address that can lie to you about the scheme."

So the one literal, copy-pasteable value in the section contradicts the two instructions bracketing it, and widens trust from the actual compose network (~65k addresses) to the whole 172.16.0.0/12 private range (~1M). DESIGN.md §4.1 states the contract as trusting X-Forwarded-Proto 'scoped to Caddy's address only'.

Impact is low today — §1.1 emits no scheme finding (src/ingest/stages/method.ts) so a spoofed X-Forwarded-Proto corrupts a dashboard claim, not a finding — which is why this is P3, not a blocker on dkz.4.

There may be a real reason for /12: Docker's default address pools are 172.17.0.0/16 … 172.31.0.0/16, all inside /12, so /12 survives a compose network being recreated with a different subnet. If that is the intent, say so and drop or reword the 'don't guess' instruction. Otherwise show the tightened value (e.g. `TRUSTED_PROXY=172.18.0.0/16`) in the dotenv block, matching what the inspect command actually prints.

Not a defect in the code: Fastify 5.8.5 scopes the header to the socket address correctly (node_modules/fastify/lib/request.js:133-137 gates on `proxyFn(socketAddr, 0)`), and the Caddyfile's reliance on Caddy replacing client-supplied X-Forwarded-* was verified empirically.
close_reason: 886902b deployment.md §3 example shows discovery output shape, no guessed CIDR

title: DESIGN.md §7 row 3.1 says 'pass otherwise' — non-z-prefixed custom objects also drive the §3.1 fail
description:
fbd22ce rewrote DESIGN.md §7 row 3.1 for 3yu. The new cell (DESIGN.md:174) reads:

  "Stage-8 semantic check, **not** the schema: fail when `z`-prefixed custom
   objects are present without the declaration, pass otherwise. ... Non-conformant
   object naming is a separate info finding."

"pass otherwise" is not what fff4987 landed. src/ingest/stages/semantic/custom-schema.ts:209:

  const custom = [...scan.custom, ...scan.misnamed];

`scan.misnamed` is the case-4 bucket: keys that are neither z-prefixed (CUSTOM_CODE, line 75) nor DS01-shaped (DS01_CODE_SHAPE, line 78) nor mis-cased known codes — e.g. `customTemp`, `zTPCM` (classify(), lines 143-152). The module header states the rule outright (lines 49-54): "4. anything else (`zTPCM`, `customTemp`) -> CUSTOM by elimination ... Cases 1 and 4 are custom objects present and drive the conditional."

So a payload carrying `customTemp` with no `meta.customDataSchema` gets a §3.1 FAIL, not the pass DESIGN promises; and the misnamed keys feed BOTH the grade and the informational naming finding (lines 240-246), not only the info finding as the cell implies.

Low severity: the shipped user-facing guidance (src/web/components/requirementReference.ts:99-100) carries the same simplification, so DESIGN is consistent with what suppliers see; but DESIGN is the doc agents re-derive the §3.1/§3.2 division of labour from, and 3yu exists precisely because that division was mis-derived once already. Suggested wording: "fail when manufacturer-specific objects (clause 4.5 `z`-prefixed, plus anything that is custom by elimination) are present without the declaration". Consider whether requirementReference 3.1 guidance should be widened in the same pass.
acceptance_criteria: DESIGN.md §7 row 3.1 (and the §6 division-of-labour paragraph if it repeats the narrowing) describes the fail set as implemented: scan.custom + scan.misnamed, not z-prefixed keys alone.
close_reason: e78e9ba/b78c0b7/c43b114/7a9ad12/9f08a60 — defect sweep: lint gate restored, DB fixtures 0.8.1 (272/272 green), empty-declaration false-PASS closed, DESIGN/README truth fixes, TxDetail evidence-based decode wording; review: all 8 pass, P3 follow-ups 3b3/2zg

title: Inspector truncation note asserts a nonexistent write-side size bound
description:
src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx:606-613 (describeStoredCopy, commit fffae12).

The stored < wire branch renders:
  'Truncated: X of Y wire bytes are stored. The drill-down copy is size-bounded and has NUL bytes stripped — this is NOT the complete payload.'

'The drill-down copy is size-bounded' is not true: cce-data-delivery-validator-1z9 establishes that no write-side cap exists — storedRawBody() only gzip-decodes and strips NUL, insertTransmission never slices, and raw_body is unbounded text. This commit adds a fourth place asserting the phantom bound (1z9 lists the DDL, src/db/repository.ts and DESIGN §8; not this file), and it contradicts fffae12's own commit message: 'instead of quoting a bound we compare the stored copy against the recorded wire_bytes and report the actual relationship'.

It also misattributes the cause. With no cap, the only way stored < wire is reachable today is NUL stripping (or a future cap). A supplier who POSTs a body containing 0x00 is told the copy was truncated by a size bound, when it was NUL-stripped.

Not a 5bs.3 acceptance break — the conclusion ('NOT the complete payload') is still correct and truncation IS disclosed — but the stated mechanism is wrong. Fix: drop the 'size-bounded' clause and name the mechanisms that actually apply (NUL stripping today; a byte cap only once 1z9 lands one). Depends on how 1z9 is resolved.
close_reason: e78e9ba/b78c0b7/c43b114/7a9ad12/9f08a60 — defect sweep: lint gate restored, DB fixtures 0.8.1 (272/272 green), empty-declaration false-PASS closed, DESIGN/README truth fixes, TxDetail evidence-based decode wording; review: all 8 pass, P3 follow-ups 3b3/2zg

title: §1.3 still described as two auth methods in the compliance matrix row and DESIGN.md
description:
5bs.4 landed Bearer end-to-end (9231ca3, e50a572) but the two places that describe §1.3 outside requirementReference still name only two methods.

1. src/api/compliance-matrix.ts:102-105 —
     { requirement: '1.3', summary: 'Auth via token header or Basic Auth (opt-in)', classes: ['verified'] }
   This summary is user-visible: ComplianceCard.tsx:390 renders row.summary as the §1.3 row headline, and ComplianceCard.tsx:348 falls back to it as the drill-down text when no REQUIREMENT_REFERENCE entry exists. A supplier who enabled Bearer from the new Setup picker sees the row that grades their Bearer traffic labelled 'token header or Basic Auth'. 5bs.4's acceptance is 'all three DS01.3 methods are offered and described accurately'; the picker and the 1.3 guidance satisfy it, this row does not.

2. DESIGN.md is stale in four places, and CLAUDE.md makes it 'the authority on scope and locked decisions':
   - DESIGN.md:193-194 §8 data model — 'auth_method (header | basic)'. This now contradicts the shipped CHECK, widened to ('header','basic','bearer') by db/initdb/50-session-auth-bearer.sql, and the AuthMethod union in src/db/repository.ts:30. An agent reading DESIGN.md §8 as the authority would reintroduce the two-value assumption.
   - DESIGN.md:149 §7 matrix row 1.3 — the row compliance-matrix.ts is 'encoded verbatim from' (compliance-matrix.ts:81-82), so item 1 cannot be fixed without fixing this first.
   - DESIGN.md:54 §3 scope table and DESIGN.md:124 §5 pipeline stage 2, both 'token header or Basic Auth'.

NOT a verbatim-quote problem: REQUIREMENT_REFERENCE['1.3'].text is a locked verbatim 2025 quote and must keep naming two (9bx explicitly forbids editing it) — these four DESIGN.md lines and the matrix summary are OUR prose about OUR service, not quotes.

Was out of the bite's declared scope only as 'docs/ churn' (9bx listed README/docs/); DESIGN.md sits at the repo root and the matrix summary is code.

Fix: add bearer to the DESIGN.md §7 row, §8 auth_method enum, §3 table and §5 pipeline line, then bring compliance-matrix.ts:103's summary back in step (e.g. 'Auth via token header, Basic, or Bearer (opt-in)').

title: ROW_ESTIMATE_PX=37 overestimates the real TxRow height (~34px), so the 10-row cap shows ~10.8 rows
description:
src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx:127-135 documents ROW_ESTIMATE_PX = 37 as '8px padding top + ~20px line box (11.5px mono) + 8px padding bottom + 1px bottom border = 37'.

The '~20px line box' term is wrong. src/web/styles.css:48 sets 'line-height: 1.5' on :root, which TxRow inherits, and the tallest span in TxRow (src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx:212, fontSize 11.5) therefore has a line box of 11.5 * 1.5 = 17.25px, not ~20px. TxRow is a flex row with alignItems:center, so the row content height is that single line box. Real row height = 8 + 17.25 + 8 + 1 = ~34.25px.

Consequence: LIST_MAX_HEIGHT_PX = ROW_ESTIMATE_PX * LIST_VISIBLE_ROWS = 370px (TransmissionsCard.tsx:164) actually exposes ~10.8 rows, not the 10 the constant name promises. measureElement corrects getTotalSize() to the real heights, so 37 has no other lasting effect - the cap is the only consumer whose accuracy depends on it.

NOT a 5bs.6 acceptance break: 10.8 is inside 'roughly 10 rows', and the detail pane still clears the fold (the height budget on LIST_MAX_HEIGHT_PX is if anything conservative). Filed so the documented derivation matches the code, since 5bs.6 deliberately made the cap depend on this number.

Fix options: correct the comment's line-box term and set ROW_ESTIMATE_PX = 34, or keep 37 as a deliberate over-estimate and say so.
close_reason: 6e51908 ROW_ESTIMATE_PX 37→34, cap coupling intact

title: Record HTTP headers and authentication outcome per transmission
description:
Lower priority — do this last (user direction, 2026-07-31).

Two related gaps in what the transmission detail can show.

1. NO HEADERS ARE STORED. db/initdb/20-transmission.sql keeps content_type and content_encoding as individual columns; the full request header set is never persisted. Showing "all recorded HTTP headers" needs a new column (new numbered DDL file per house rule) plus repository and API threading.

   SECURITY DESIGN REQUIRED BEFORE ANY DDL: the Authorization header carries the credential THIS SERVICE ISSUED to the supplier. Storing headers verbatim writes that secret into the datastore and then renders it in a dashboard reachable by anyone holding the capability URL. DESIGN.md section 12 already commits to auth secrets being "stored hashed, never echoed after first display" — verbatim header capture would violate that. Needs a redaction policy (which headers are captured, which are masked, whether the masking is visible) decided before implementation.

2. FAILED AUTH IS INVISIBLE. src/ingest/stages/auth.ts sits BEFORE the persistence boundary and halts 401 without writing a transmission row. A supplier debugging a credential sees literally nothing in the dashboard — no row, no finding, no evidence the request arrived. Answering "was this transmission authenticated?" well means deciding whether to persist rejected attempts at all, which is a change to the pipeline contract (DESIGN.md section 6), not just a new column.

   Note the ordering wrinkle already documented in auth.ts: stage 0 bumps last_post_at before auth runs, so a 401 already stamps session activity for the retention clock. Persisting the row would make that consistent.

Consider whether a simple derived "authenticated: yes/no/not-required" field on the detail pane — computed from the existing section 1.3 finding — delivers most of the value without either change. That would ship today; full header capture would not.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on header redaction and on whether 401s persist; the transmission detail can answer "was this authenticated?"; no issued credential is stored or displayed in the clear.

title: Add CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md
description:
Neither file exists.

SECURITY.md is the more important of the two here. This is a public, unauthenticated-by-default service that mints bearer capability URLs, where possession of a UUID grants both write (POST transmissions) and destructive (DELETE session) authority. DESIGN.md section 12 already enumerates the accepted risks honestly - capability URLs leaking via logs/proxies/browser history, hashed auth secrets, the 1MB cap and zip-bomb guard. What is missing is a coordinated-disclosure path for anyone who finds something the design did not anticipate. It should also restate the synthetic-data-only boundary, since the security posture depends entirely on it.

CONTRIBUTING.md should cover the conventions an outside contributor cannot guess:
  - Node 20+, ESM, TypeScript end-to-end.
  - Tests colocate as *.test.ts and run on the Node test runner via tsx --test - NOT Jest or Vitest.
  - Postgres required for the full suite (see the CI issue).
  - DDL goes in new numbered files under db/initdb/, never edited in place.
  - Schemas are vendored and pinned by content hash; adding a version means registering blessed bytes, never editing an existing file.
  - Where prose requirements and the JSON schema disagree, the schema wins (requirement 3.2) - except data-object bounds and units, where Annex 1 is authoritative.
  - Issue tracking uses bd (beads), which will be unfamiliar to most contributors and needs a short orientation or an alternative intake path.

That last point deserves a decision: outside contributors will expect the hosting platform issue tracker, not a local beads database with no remote.
acceptance_criteria: SECURITY.md gives a disclosure path and restates the synthetic-data boundary; CONTRIBUTING.md covers the non-obvious conventions; the issue-intake path for outside contributors is decided and stated.

title: NEXT BITE: clear 4h4 review follow-ups (l09 chip removal + ktx doc)
description:
## Underlying issues

- cce-data-delivery-validator-l09 (P3, task): ComplianceCard still renders the legacy "From transmissions" per-tx chip wall BELOW the new signature rows added by 4h4.11 — remove it.
- cce-data-delivery-validator-ktx (P3, task): TransmissionsCard `failuresOnly` prop doc comment still says "NOT yet rendered" though 4h4.12 rendered the checkbox — fix the stale comment.

Both surfaced by the clean-context review of the 4h4.10/11/12+3ta bite (commits ff0ad93 / 5511657+dbdbf2f / acb7faa / 58c26aa).

## Read first

Memories:
- `bd memories schema` (`schema-registry-0.8.1-current-outdated`) — only if touching signature rendering during the l09 removal; the outdated-schema `sev:info` → `--mixed` rule still holds. Not load-bearing for the chip removal itself.

Code:
- `src/web/components/ComplianceCard.tsx:468` — `renderContributingChips` ("From transmissions") section (lines ~468-473) + the `renderContributingChips` fn (~492). This is what l09 removes. The new `SignatureSummary` (added by 4h4.11) sits directly above it and is the intended replacement.
- `src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx:31-35` — the `failuresOnly` prop doc; ktx rewrites it to match the sibling props (`onToggleFailuresOnly`/`activeSignature`/`onClearSignature`/`visibleCount`/`scopedTotal`), whose "NOT yet" caveats 4h4.12 already dropped. The checkbox lives at ~line 479-484.
- Epic `cce-data-delivery-validator-4h4` acceptance: "requirements show deduped signature issues NOT per-tx chips" — this is the contract l09 satisfies.

## Recently-decided context

**DESIGN TENSION to resolve, not silently inherit (the whole reason this is a NEXT BITE):**

The just-executed bite (7g6) recently-decided context #2 said: "ComplianceCard still gets the summary full `data.transmissions` for its existing From transmissions chips" — i.e. it told the 4h4.11 implementer to KEEP the chips. That instruction was WRONG and contradicts (a) 4h4.11 own WHY ("a requirement failing on 180 transmissions rendered 180 chips; signatures collapse that to a few distinct issues") and (b) the epic acceptance ("deduped signature issues NOT per-tx chips"). The card currently renders BOTH — re-introducing the 180-chip scale failure the epic set out to kill.

DEFAULT DECISION (defensible, follow unless the user overrides): REMOVE the chip wall per l09. The signature rows are the replacement. After removal, ComplianceCard can also drop its dependence on the full `transmissions` array for the EXPANDED detail (keep `transmissions` only for whatever row-chrome / header counts still need it — verify before deleting the prop usage; do not break `{f}f {p}p` counts or the StatusPill).

If the user wants the chips KEPT (e.g. as a collapsed "show raw transmissions" affordance), this becomes a redesign, not a deletion — stop and confirm before building that.

## Slicing recommendation

Two FILE-DISJOINT slices. Trivial enough for ONE agent doing both serially, OR two parallel agents (no shared file).

1. **l09 — ComplianceCard chip removal**
   - Edits ONLY `src/web/components/ComplianceCard.tsx`.
   - Remove the "From transmissions" chip section (~468-473) + `renderContributingChips` fn (~492). Then check whether `transmissions` is still needed for expanded detail; if not, simplify the prop usage WITHOUT breaking row chrome / counts / the §req cross-link.
   - Acceptance: expanded requirement shows ONLY the SignatureSummary (no per-tx chip wall); row chrome, grouping, counts, StatusPill, §req link unchanged.

2. **ktx — TransmissionsCard doc comment**
   - Edits ONLY `src/web/components/TransmissionsCard.tsx`.
   - Rewrite the `failuresOnly` doc comment (~31-35) to match the sibling props (drop "NOT yet rendered"; state the checkbox is wired). Doc-only, no functional change.
   - Acceptance: comment matches the sibling seam-prop comments; no behavior change.

Run order: parallel (different files) or one serial agent. Within l09, removal then prop-cleanup is sequential in the same file.

## Out of scope

- `4h4.13` virtualization (separate P3, completes the epic — do NOT bundle here).
- `to8` SSE push, `ven` standard-revision proposals.
- Any styles.css / api.ts / Dashboard.tsx / backend edits. No new tokens.
- Re-designing the chips into a collapsed affordance (only if the user overrides the removal default — confirm first).

## Commit + test expectations

- `src/web/` work. Verify BEFORE commit: `npm run typecheck:web`, `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `npm run lint` (run `npm run format` if prettier flags, then re-scope `git add`). No web test infra — typecheck/lint is the binding gate. Run the FULL-TREE lint, not just isolated — the prior bite shipped a prettier miss because agents verified in isolation.
- Commit per underlying issue when green (no push). Terse style ending `(l09)` / `(ktx)`; `git log --oneline -5` first. Scope `git add` to your file; the beads pre-commit hook re-exports `.beads/issues.jsonl` (benign) — do NOT use --no-verify.
- Close each underlying issue with its sha. After both land, the epic 4h4 acceptance gap on "not per-tx chips" is closed (epic still open pending 4h4.13 virtualization).
close_reason: l09 (0d43633) + ktx (5bcf907) landed; gates green; reviewer no defects; epic 4h4 'not per-tx chips' acceptance gap closed

title: NEXT BITE: epic 108 P3 polish — scroll/in-flight/tx-chips
description:
## Underlying issues

- cce-data-delivery-validator-b6u (P3 bug): gfx reveal scrollIntoView no-ops on the cross-link it targets (runs same tick as the un-hide setters).
- cce-data-delivery-validator-rh3 (P3 task): Delete-modal confirmDelete lacks an in-flight guard — rapid double-click double-fires deleteSessionData.
- cce-data-delivery-validator-i7c (P3 task): ComplianceCard drill-down omits the "From transmissions" chips (renderContributingChips returns null).
- (closes) cce-data-delivery-validator-108 (EPIC, P2): 10/10 children done; close after these polish items land.

These are the residual P3 follow-ups from epic 108 (the reviewer-filed defects b6u/rh3 + the documented i7c gap). All deps met; web-only, no backend.

## Read first

- `bd memories dashboard` / `bd memories redesign` — epic philosophy: reuse the real data flow; NO client-side reclassification of the compliance summary.
- `design_handoff_validator_redesign/README.md` → "## Interactions & Behavior" (ComplianceCard bullet) for the "From transmissions" chip behavior; the prototype derives contributing txs by walking findings.
- `design_handoff_validator_redesign/redesign/proto-ui.jsx` — chip rendering reference for i7c.
- `src/web/components/ComplianceCard.tsx` — reveal effect (~296-302, b6u), renderContributingChips (~239-255, i7c), CompliancePaneProps interface (~28-46), ReqRow (selectedTx/onSelectTx already threaded), groupForRow/isCollapsed helpers.
- `src/web/routes/Dashboard.tsx` — confirmDelete (~244-255) + closeDeleteModal (~235) + DeleteModal JSX (~442-449) for rh3; the ComplianceCard JSX (~420-431) for i7c (NOTE: transmissions is passed to TransmissionsCard at ~432, NOT to ComplianceCard yet).
- `src/web/components/DeleteModal.tsx` — DeleteModalProps (open/count/value/onChange/onCancel/onConfirm); rh3 adds a pending/disabled state.
- `src/web/api.ts` — TransmissionView (id + embedded findings: FindingView[] with .requirement); ComplianceRow (requirement + classes + counts, NO tx ids). Confirms i7c derivation source.

## Recently-decided context (preserve precisely)

1. i7c APPROACH = FRONTEND DERIVATION (decided this session). The data already exists: SessionResponse.transmissions[].findings[].requirement. Contributing txs for a row = transmissions.filter(tx => tx.findings.some(f => f.requirement === row.requirement)). Chip click → onSelectTx(tx.id); selectedTx marks the active chip (both props ALREADY threaded through ComplianceCard + ReqRow). This is NOT reclassification (just finding→tx navigation linkage), so it does NOT violate the epic the "no client-side reclassification of the summary" rule. Do NOT add a backend/summary-response change; the prototype walked findings the same way.
2. i7c COUPLES TWO FILES: Dashboard.tsx must add transmissions={transmissions} to the <ComplianceCard> JSX (~420-431), and ComplianceCard.tsx must add `transmissions: TransmissionView[]` to CompliancePaneProps + implement renderContributingChips using it. Dashboard.tsx has NO separate CompliancePaneProps mirror (the ComplianceCard comment saying "EXACT copy of Dashboard.tsx" is historical) — the interface edit is ComplianceCard-only. This two-file overlap is why i7c was deferred out of the prior bite (1mt) and why it must run LAST here.
3. b6u FIX is ComplianceCard-internal only. The reveal effect (~296-302) calls onToggleGroup/onShowNonGradeableChange then scrollIntoView in the SAME tick, so the row is not yet in the DOM. Defer the scroll: a second useEffect keyed on expandedReq + the now-current collapsed/filter state, OR requestAnimationFrame after the toggles. The data-req attribute already exists on the row. Keep the existing reveal (un-collapse + un-filter) — only the scroll timing changes.
4. rh3 FIX spans Dashboard.tsx + DeleteModal.tsx. Add a `deleting` flag in Dashboard (useState); confirmDelete returns early if already deleting, sets it true before the call, clears it in finally (or on close). Pass a `deleting`/`pending` prop into DeleteModal and disable the red "Delete everything" button (and ignore re-entry) while pending. The existing arm-on-DELETE logic stays.

## Slicing recommendation

Two steps. Step 1 is fully parallel (disjoint files); Step 2 is serial because it edits BOTH files Step 1 touched.

### Step 1 — PARALLEL (no shared files)

1. **Slice A — b6u (ComplianceCard.tsx ONLY)**
   - Reads: ComplianceCard.tsx reveal effect (~296-302), data-req attribute on ReqRow.
   - Produces: deferred scrollIntoView (rAF or second effect) so the row is in the DOM before scrolling; reveal (un-collapse/un-filter) unchanged.
   - Acceptance: clicking a finding §req for a default-collapsed/filtered requirement scrolls that exact row into view on first click; no render loop; build:web + lint green.

2. **Slice B — rh3 (Dashboard.tsx + DeleteModal.tsx)**
   - Reads: Dashboard confirmDelete/closeDeleteModal/DeleteModal JSX; DeleteModalProps.
   - Produces: a `deleting` in-flight flag in Dashboard (early-return re-entry guard + try/finally), a new `deleting`/`pending` prop on DeleteModal that disables the confirm button while pending.
   - Acceptance: rapid double-click fires deleteSessionData at most once; button is visibly disabled while pending; successful delete still closes+clears+refetches; build:web + lint green.

### Step 2 — SERIAL after BOTH A and B commit

3. **Slice C — i7c (Dashboard.tsx + ComplianceCard.tsx)**
   - Reads: api.ts TransmissionView/FindingView/ComplianceRow; ComplianceCard renderContributingChips (~239) + CompliancePaneProps; Dashboard ComplianceCard JSX; proto-ui.jsx chip layout.
   - Produces: add transmissions to CompliancePaneProps + pass it from Dashboard; implement renderContributingChips to derive contributing txs per the decided filter and render a chip per tx (onSelectTx(tx.id), selectedTx = active). Match proto-ui chip styling.
   - Acceptance: a requirement drill-down shows a "From transmissions" chip per contributing tx; clicking a chip selects that tx in the right pane (selectedTx updates, chip marks active); requirements with no contributing tx render no chip section; build:web + lint green.

Run order: A ∥ B (parallel), THEN C. C shares ComplianceCard.tsx with A and Dashboard.tsx with B, so it MUST wait for both to commit. Do NOT parallelize C with either.

## Out of scope

- Backend/summary-response changes for i7c (frontend derivation only — decision above).
- to8 (SSE push) and ven (standard-revision proposals) — unrelated P3 features, separate threads.
- styles.css, ui/* internals, api.ts (read-only here), TransmissionsCard, Setup, the poll/visibility/refetch logic.
- Do NOT touch the compliance summary computation or rollup (no reclassification).

## Commit + test expectations

- Gate per commit: `npm run build:web` (typecheck:web + vite) GREEN + `npm run lint` (eslint + prettier --check) CLEAN. Run `npm run format` if prettier complains, then re-lint. No push (local-only).
- Each slice commits ONLY its own files via explicit pathspec (`git commit -- <paths>`); on `.git/index.lock` contention wait+retry (do not delete the lock).
- One commit per slice, terse style (git log --oneline first): e.g. "Defer cross-link scroll until target row renders (b6u)", "Guard delete confirm against double-fire (rh3)", "Derive From-transmissions chips in ComplianceCard drill-down (i7c)".
- After all three land, close b6u/rh3/i7c AND close epic cce-data-delivery-validator-108 (10/10 children done; these were the residual P3 polish).

title: Push dashboard updates via Server-Sent Events (SSE)
description:
Follow-up to cce-data-delivery-validator-qkc (which ships visibility-aware client polling). Replace/augment polling with near-instant push: add GET /api/sessions/:uuid/events returning text/event-stream. The ingest handler (src/ingest/route.js) emits a per-uuid event after each transmission is persisted; the client opens an EventSource and refetches (or applies a delta) on each message.

Open questions to resolve first:
- Deployment topology: an in-process EventEmitter pub/sub only works single-instance. If multi-replica behind a load balancer, the SSE connection and the ingest POST can land on different instances — needs Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY or Redis pub/sub to fan out.

title: 404 handler: callNotFound() inside setNotFoundHandler degrades API 404s to plain text + logs warning
description:
When the web SPA build exists (production/docker image), buildApp() registers a custom setNotFoundHandler (src/app.ts:164-169). For a non-GET request, or any unmatched API path, it calls reply.callNotFound() FROM INSIDE the notFoundHandler. This is a Fastify anti-pattern: Fastify logs 'Trying to send a NotFound error inside a 404 handler. Sending basic 404 response.' (warn) and returns a degraded body.

REPRO (docker compose up):
  curl -i -XPOST -d '{}' http://localhost:3000/some-unknown-path
  curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/unknown
Both return: HTTP 404, Content-Type text/plain, body '404 Not Found' — and emit a warn log line each.

EXPECTED (per the code comment 'fall through to Fastify default 404/405'): Fastify's standard JSON 404, e.g. {"statusCode":404,"error":"Not Found","message":"Route POST:/some-unknown-path not found"}, and NO warning.

IMPACT: low. Every API/non-GET 404 returns a degraded plain-text body (broken API error contract) and adds warn-level log noise. Only manifests when webDist exists (SPA fallback registered) — i.e. the production image, not the no-web test path. Surfaced while driving the validator with the ems-data-simulator: posting to the wrong path (bare uuid instead of /i/<uuid>) hit this.

FIX: do not call reply.callNotFound() within the notFoundHandler. For the non-SPA branch, send the 404 directly, e.g. reply.code(404).send({statusCode:404,error:'Not Found',message:`Route ${request.method}:${request.url} not found`}) (or reply.callNotFound only via a separate, non-recursive path). Add a test asserting POST /unknown and GET /api/unknown return JSON 404 with no warning.
acceptance_criteria: POST to an unknown path and GET to an unknown /api path return Fastify's JSON 404 body (statusCode/error/message) with Content-Type application/json and emit no 'NotFound error inside a 404 handler' warning; GET /d/<uuid> still serves the SPA index.html.
close_reason: Fixed in src/app.ts: replaced reply.callNotFound() inside setNotFoundHandler (the re-entrant anti-pattern) with a direct Fastify-shaped JSON 404 ({statusCode,error,message}). Added regression tests in src/app.web.test.ts (POST /unknown and GET /api/unknown -> JSON 404, no SPA shell). Verified on rebuilt docker image: POST/GET unknown paths return application/json 404 with zero 'NotFound error inside a 404 handler' warnings; /d/:uuid still serves index.html. typecheck + lint + 8/8 web tests green.

title: NEXT BITE: M8 polish — teaching-surface body + fixture tests
description:
## Underlying issues

- cce-data-delivery-validator-bat.2: Error messaging / teaching surfaces — polish the ingest response body + human-readable error/finding messages (DESIGN.md §6, §14.8).
- cce-data-delivery-validator-bat.1: Fixture transmissions as tests — valid payload + one fixture per conditional failure case (DESIGN.md §14.8).
- Parent epic: cce-data-delivery-validator-bat (Polish & fixtures, M8). This is the LAST v1 implementation milestone.

## Read first

Documents:

- DESIGN.md §6 (lines 108-131) — the ordered ingest stages, response codes, and the explicit "success body is a teaching surface — echo finding count" note. The canonical spec for both tasks.
- DESIGN.md §7 (lines 132-171) — the verifiability matrix; requirement ids (1.4, 1.2, 1.6, 1.1, 3.2, 1.8) that findings reference via `requirement`.

Code (read before editing):

- src/ingest/pipeline.ts:153 — `buildResponseBody(status, findings, transmissionId)` currently returns `{ transmissionId, status, findings: <count> }`. THIS is the teaching surface bat.2 must enrich.
- src/ingest/pipeline.ts:18-60 — `Finding` = `InsertFindingInput` = `{ requirement, severity: 'pass'|'fail'|'info', detail?, pointer? }`. NOTE: findings carry `detail` (human-readable) and `requirement`, but NO machine `code` field. Message polish builds off `detail`.
- src/ingest/route.ts — wiring; persistence boundary (404/405 persist no row; stage 3+ always persist).
- src/ingest/route.test.ts — full-flow test conventions: node:test + node:assert/strict, the `{ skip }` DB-guard idiom (skips when no Postgres reachable).
- src/ingest/stages/{size,content-type,encoding,parse,schema,semantic}.ts — where each finding is produced; the source of the messages bat.2 polishes.

## Recently-decided context

Facts established this session by reading the code (not yet in the issue descriptions):

- **Six conditional-failure fixtures map to specific stages/codes:** oversize → 413 (size stage), bad content-type → finding/415 (content-type), illegal double-encoding → 400 (encoding), unparseable → 400 (parse), schema-invalid → 422 (schema), duplicate transferId → 2xx + finding (semantic). bat.1 needs one fixture each + the valid baseline (200).
- **Ordering constraint between the two tasks:** bat.2 changes the shape returned by `buildResponseBody`. bat.1's end-to-end tests assert on that response body. So bat.2 must land FIRST (lock the response shape), THEN bat.1 writes assertions against the finalized shape. Running bat.1 first would force a rewrite.
- **DB dependence splits the test strategy:** any test that POSTs to `/i/:uuid` and reaches stage 3+ persists a row → needs Postgres → MUST use the existing skip-guard idiom from route.test.ts / repository.test.ts. Pre-body cases (405, and pipeline-level unit tests calling `runPipeline` against a hand-built context) can run WITHOUT a DB. Prefer pipeline-level fixture tests where possible so they run in CI without Postgres; reserve DB-skip tests for true end-to-end persistence assertions.
- **Only one bd memory exists** (M4 frontend stack); there is no ingest/teaching-surface memory to consult — DESIGN.md + the code above are the source of truth.

## Slicing recommendation

1. **Subagent A — bat.2 (error messaging / teaching surfaces)**
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §6/§7, src/ingest/pipeline.ts, src/ingest/route.ts, the stage files for current `detail` strings.
   - Produces: enriched `buildResponseBody` (e.g. include a human-readable summary message + per-finding `{requirement, severity, detail}` so suppliers see results without the dashboard, per the §6 teaching-surface note) and polished/consistent finding `detail` messages across stages. Unit tests in pipeline.test.ts for the new body shape.
   - Acceptance: `npm test` green (no-DB pipeline tests cover the new body shape); response body documented in the function's doc comment; no widening of `PipelineContext`.
   - Touches: src/ingest/pipeline.ts (+ maybe route.ts), stage files, pipeline.test.ts.

2. **Subagent B — bat.1 (fixture transmissions as tests)** — runs AFTER A.
   - Reads: the FINAL response shape A produced; route.test.ts skip-guard idiom; the six stage→code mappings above.
   - Produces: a fixtures set (valid + 6 failure cases) under e.g. src/ingest/fixtures/ and tests asserting each yields the right status code + findings. Use pipeline-level `runPipeline` assertions where no DB is needed; DB-skip-guarded end-to-end POST tests for persistence.
   - Acceptance: `npm test` green with and without Postgres (DB cases skip cleanly when unreachable); all seven cases covered; assertions match A's finalized body shape.
   - Touches: new fixtures dir + route.test.ts / a new test file.

Run order: **SERIAL — A then B.** B's assertions depend on A's response shape; both may touch pipeline.test.ts / the ingest test surface, so they cannot run in parallel safely.

## Out of scope

- **cce-data-delivery-validator-ven** (standard-revision proposals) — upstream WHO-stewarded standard suggestions, a doc artifact, explicitly non-blocking for v1. NOT part of M8 implementation. Leave it open.
- **Active conformance harness (§4) and guided retransmission scenarios (§5)** — the 🔌 "active-only (deferred)" matrix rows. Do not build error-injection or retry-measurement machinery.
- Do NOT edit the vendored schema (src/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.0.json) — it is content-hash-pinned (DESIGN.md §9); the stale `0.1.1` example is an upstream fix tracked in ven.
- Do not widen `PipelineContext` to carry response-message state (route.ts comment calls this out).

## Commit + test expectations

title: NEXT BITE: M7 retention worker (yhg.1)
description:
## Underlying issues

- yhg.1: Retention worker — periodic purge of sessions whose COALESCE(last_post_at, created_at) is older than 30 days, cascading to transmissions/findings (DESIGN.md §11).
- yhg: [epic] Retention & lifecycle (M7). Its SECOND deliverable — "expiry surfaced in the dashboard" — is ALREADY DONE (src/web/components/Lifecycle.tsx / yih.5 + GET returns expiresAt). This bite is WORKER-ONLY; the epic closes once yhg.1 lands.

This is DESIGN §14 build-order step 7 (M7). M2–M6 are all landed (M6 §1.3 auth just closed at a9de047/68d0fed/18d937a).

## Read first

Memory:
- `bd memories` holds only the M4 frontend-stack decision — NOT relevant here (this is backend/worker only, no web change). Auto-memory architecture-decisions.md notes the 30-day retention scope but the DESIGN section below suffices.

Documents / code:
- DESIGN.md §11 (the whole section — 4 lines): a periodic worker deletes sessions (cascade to transmissions/findings) whose last_post_at (or created_at if no posts) is older than 30 days; expiry is surfaced in the dashboard (already done).
- db/initdb/10-session.sql, 20-transmission.sql, 30-finding.sql — the FK cascade is ALREADY wired: transmission REFERENCES session ON DELETE CASCADE, finding REFERENCES transmission ON DELETE CASCADE. So purging is a SINGLE `DELETE FROM session WHERE ...` — do NOT write per-table deletes; the DB cascades. NO schema change.
- src/api/sessions.ts:37-38,183-184 — the retention contract the worker MUST mirror exactly: `RETENTION_MS = 30*24*60*60*1000`, base = `last_post_at ?? created_at`, expiresAt = base + RETENTION_MS. The dashboard countdown (Lifecycle.tsx) is computed from this. The purge predicate must agree: delete when `COALESCE(last_post_at, created_at) < now() - 30 days`. If they diverge, the dashboard says "expires in N days" while the row is already gone (or vice versa).
- src/db/repository.ts — the repository idiom: typed wrappers, injectable `db?` param (default getPool()), e.g. bumpLastPostAt at :359-371. The purge fn belongs here and follows this idiom (injectable db for DB-gated tests).
- src/db/pool.ts (getPool/closePool), src/db/index.ts (barrel — export the new fn here).
- src/app.ts (buildApp factory, BuildAppOptions at :75) and src/index.ts (listen/bootstrap entrypoint). There is NO existing background-task/setInterval/cron pattern in the repo — see Recently-decided for the execution model.
- Test idiom: DB-gated tests skip gracefully when no Postgres is reachable (see the *.test.ts files for the skip pattern, e.g. sessions/auth-stage tests). The pure purge fn gets DB-gated coverage; do not depend on a live timer in tests.

## Recently-decided context (this session, not yet in yhg.1)

- **Dashboard expiry display is ALREADY COMPLETE** (Lifecycle.tsx, yih.5; GET returns expiresAt). Do NOT touch the web or the sessions API. This bite adds ONLY the purge worker. The epic's two-part scope is now one-part.
- **Cascade is pre-wired in SQL** — the worker is one `DELETE FROM session WHERE COALESCE(last_post_at, created_at) < now() - interval '30 days'` (or parameterized with RETENTION_MS). transmissions + findings cascade automatically. Verify the cascade exists; do NOT add manual child deletes and do NOT change the schema.
- **Purge predicate MUST mirror src/api/sessions.ts** (base = last_post_at ?? created_at; window = 30 days = RETENTION_MS). Consider exporting/sharing the 30-day constant so display and purge cannot drift. Returning the count of purged sessions (DELETE ... RETURNING / rowCount) is useful for logging/tests.
- **Execution-model recommendation (genuine fork — flag if you disagree):** the deployment is a single docker-compose app process (Fastify via index.ts→buildApp→listen) + Postgres + Caddy; there is NO separate scheduler service. RECOMMENDED: split into (1) a pure, directly-testable `purgeExpiredSessions(db?)` repository fn (the unit of test, DB-gated), and (2) a thin periodic scheduler (setInterval) started at boot in index.ts (NOT in buildApp — keep buildApp port-free and side-effect-free so app.inject tests do not spawn timers), with a configurable interval (env, e.g. RETENTION_SWEEP_MS) and an unref()'d timer so it never blocks process exit. Run one sweep shortly after boot. ALTERNATIVE (if preferred): a standalone `scripts/retention-worker` one-shot invoked by an external cron/compose service — bigger surface, defer unless the user wants it. Pick the in-process default unless instructed otherwise.

## Slicing recommendation

Small, cohesive, single-file-ish change — **one general-purpose subagent, serial.** No parallelism needed.

1. **Subagent A — retention worker (yhg.1)**
   - Reads: DESIGN §11; db/initdb/*.sql (confirm cascade); src/api/sessions.ts:37-38,183-184 (retention contract); src/db/repository.ts (idiom + bumpLastPostAt example), src/db/index.ts, src/db/pool.ts; src/index.ts + src/app.ts (boot wiring); an existing *.test.ts for the DB-gated skip idiom.
   - Produces: `purgeExpiredSessions(db?)` in src/db/repository.ts (single cascading DELETE, returns purged count), exported via src/db/index.ts; a thin periodic scheduler started in src/index.ts (setInterval, configurable interval, unref'd, one sweep after boot, logs purged count) — NOT in buildApp; DB-gated unit test asserting an old session (+ its transmissions/findings) is purged and a fresh one survives, skipping gracefully with no DB.
   - Acceptance: a session with COALESCE(last_post_at, created_at) older than 30 days is deleted and its transmissions/findings cascade-delete; a recent session is untouched; predicate matches the dashboard's base+window; buildApp stays side-effect-free (no timer in inject tests); `npm run build && npm test && npm run lint` green.

## Out of scope

- **The web / dashboard expiry display** — already done (Lifecycle.tsx, yih.5). Do NOT touch src/web/* or the sessions API.
- **DB schema / cascade changes** — the FK cascade already exists; verify only.
- **buildApp side effects** — do NOT start the timer inside buildApp (would spawn timers in every app.inject test). Boot-only wiring in index.ts.
- **A separate scheduler service / external cron** — the in-process default is sufficient for v1; only build the standalone-script variant if the user asks.
- **Soft-delete / archival / audit log of purges** — not in §11; a hard cascading DELETE is the spec.
- **M8 polish (bat), schema-revision proposals (ven)** — separate milestones.

## Commit + test expectations

- Commit to this repo (local-only; no remote → do NOT push). Terse `<prefix>: <summary> (yhg.1)` style — check `git log --oneline` first. Suggested: `retention: purge sessions inactive >30 days (yhg.1)`.
- Verify gates green BEFORE committing: `npm run build && npm test && npm run lint` (`npm run format` fixes style). `git add` only the touched files (do NOT `git add -A`; the beads pre-commit hook may re-stage .beads/issues.jsonl — expected).
- No `bd close` by the implementer — the coordinator closes after the clean-context review.

title: Standard-revision proposals: schemaVersion identity, no-runtime-fetch, content-hash manifest
description:
Upstream suggestions for the next WHO-stewarded revision of the Interoperable CCE Data Delivery schema/standard. Not blocking v1 (our tool handles today's ambiguity via normalization — see DESIGN.md §9), but worth proposing since the standard is being revised.

Proposals:
1. Make meta.schemaVersion an explicit, opaque bare-semver token (e.g. "0.8.0") and state in prose it is an identifier the receiver maps to a schema via its own registry — decoupled from hosting. Drop the 'see the $id field' phrasing that conflates identifier with locator.
2. State that receivers MUST NOT dereference the schema at validation time and SHOULD validate against a pre-registered copy (availability, SSRF, and provability reasons).
3. Mechanically link $id and schemaVersion so there is exactly one version string and a deterministic way to derive one from the other.
4. Publish an out-of-band manifest with a content hash (sha256) per version, so any receiver can prove it holds the blessed bytes.
5. Fix the stale example: schemaVersion.examples is "0.1.1" (annotation-only, ignored by validators). Must be fixed upstream, NOT in our vendored copy, since we pin that file by content hash (DESIGN.md §9).

Context: DESIGN.md §9 (schema registry) and §15 (deferred).
notes:
EVIDENCE 2026-07-31 for proposals 1-4: the published $id (https://schemas.2to8.cc/schemas/cce-interop-<version>.json) points at a host that DOES NOT RESOLVE. The artifact is actually served from https://docs.2to8.cc/cce-data-interop/schemas/cce-interop-<version>.json - different host AND path. Any receiver treating $id as a locator gets a DNS failure. This is a live, demonstrable defect to cite when proposing the identifier/locator split and the content-hash manifest. Partly overtaken by plan: maintainer intends to change $id to a URN, which implements proposal 1 directly. Proposal 5 (stale 0.1.1 example) is already fixed in the published 0.8.1.
Update from 5bs.1 work (fff4987, 2026-08-01): the upstream gap has partially closed. Published cce-interop-0.8.2 (sha256 b6ee10cf…) defines $defs/custom-data-schema, referenced from transmission-metadata.properties.customDataSchema (by-reference URL, inline schema with versioned $id, or array of either), NOT in required, and its $comment states the conditional is 'deliberately NOT enforced by this schema … Employers wishing to enforce it should do so in their own validation layer' — i.e. upstream explicitly delegates enforcement to receiving systems like this one. Vendored+published 0.8.1 remain byte-identical (290290fd…) and lack the field. Our §3.1 stage grades the conditional schema-independently, so it works for 0.8.1 traffic today and 0.8.2 later.
